definition_zh: 抽象的；理论上的；摘要；提取；抽象艺术作品
definition_en: existing as an idea rather than a physical thing, a summary of a paper, or to draw something out
core_image: 从具体事物里抽出一根最关键的线，剩下的细节被拿走
scene: 画室里，画家把桌上的水果简化成几块纯色方形，不再管光影和纹理。She prefers abstract shapes to realistic detail.
sceneCN: 这里 abstract 是「抽象的」（第 1 个义项：只以观念形态存在，不描摹实物）；句意为她偏爱抽象形状胜过写实细节。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「抽象地」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「心不在焉的」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「抽象；抽象概念」

senses.title: Existing only as an idea
senses.definition: describing something that exists as an idea or quality rather than a physical object
senses.definitionCN: 指以观念或性质而非实体形式存在的事物
senses.example: Justice is an abstract concept until a law gives it shape.
senses.exampleCN: 在法律赋予形状之前，正义只是一个抽象概念。
senses.why: Latin abstractus means 'drawn away'; the mind draws the quality away from the object and keeps only the idea.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abstractus 意为「被抽走的」；心智把性质从事物中抽走，只留下观念。

senses.title: Theoretical rather than practical
senses.definition: dealing with general theory instead of concrete cases
senses.definitionCN: 处理一般理论而非具体情形
senses.example: The argument stays abstract because it never names a real case.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证始终停留在抽象层面，因为从未举出真实案例。
senses.why: Once a discussion loses touch with examples, it drifts into the drawn-away realm, so abstract comes to mean impractical.
senses.whyCN: 一旦讨论脱离实例，就漂进那个「被抽走」的领域，于是 abstract 引申为不切实际。

senses.title: A summary of a paper
senses.definition: a short statement that sums up the contents of an article or paper
senses.definitionCN: 概括文章或论文内容的简短说明
senses.example: Read the abstract before you decide to cite the study.
senses.exampleCN: 决定引用这项研究前，先读摘要。
senses.why: A summary is literally drawn out of the whole text: the essential parts are taken away and set at the front.
senses.whyCN: 摘要是从全文里「抽出来」的：要点被取走并放在文章前面。

senses.title: To draw something out
senses.definition: to remove or separate something, especially a substance or a quality
senses.definitionCN: 移出或分离某物，尤指物质或性质
senses.example: Chemists abstract the oil from the seeds with a solvent.
senses.exampleCN: 化学家用溶剂从种子中提取油脂。
senses.why: Here the literal Latin sense survives: a part is physically taken out of the whole that contains it.
senses.whyCN: 这里保留了拉丁语的字面义：一部分被从包含它的整体中实际取出来。

senses.title: An abstract work of art
senses.definition: a painting or sculpture that does not represent recognizable objects
senses.definitionCN: 不表现可辨认物象的绘画或雕塑
senses.example: The gallery hung three large abstracts beside the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊在入口旁挂了三幅大幅抽象画。
senses.why: When artists stop copying objects and keep only shapes and colours, the noun names the finished work of that removal.
senses.whyCN: 当艺术家不再描摹物体、只保留形状与色彩，名词就指这种「抽离」完成后的作品。

intro.en: Abstract comes from Latin abstrahere, 'to draw away', built from trahere, 'to pull'.
intro.cn: abstract 来自拉丁语 abstrahere（抽走），由 trahere（拉）构成。

items.en: trahere meant 'to draw, pull', and it also gave tractor and attract.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖」，也衍生出 tractor 与 attract。

items.en: The prefix abs- meant 'away from', shortened from ab.
items.cn: 前缀 abs- 意为「离开」，是 ab 的缩略形式。

items.en: abstractus was the past participle, literally 'drawn away'.
items.cn: abstractus 是过去分词，字面意为「被抽走的」。

items.en: Scholastic writers used abstractus for qualities considered apart from the objects that hold them.
items.cn: 经院作家用 abstractus 指脱离承载物而被考虑的性质。

items.en: English abstract first described a quality taken out of a substance, then a summary of a text.
items.cn: 英语 abstract 先指从实体中抽出的性质，后指文章的摘要。

items.en: Modern usage adds abstract art and the verb for chemical extraction.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了抽象艺术，以及表示化学提取的动词。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the same Latin pulling root; the second gathers words for ideas and summaries.
note.cn: 第一组收建立在同一拉丁「拉」词根上的词；第二组收表示观念与摘要的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of abstracting or the resulting general idea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「抽象行为」或由此产生的「抽象概念」。

entries.definition: To pull something toward oneself, from the same Latin trahere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吸引」，同出拉丁语 trahere。

entries.definition: A machine that pulls, literally a puller.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「拖拉机」，字面即「拉的东西」。

entries.definition: An agreement, literally something drawn together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「合同」，字面是「拉到一起的东西」。

entries.definition: An adjective for ideas tested in thought rather than in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「理论的」，在思想而非实践中检验的观念。

entries.definition: An adjective for something that cannot be touched.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无形的、不可触摸的」。

entries.definition: A short account of the main points of a longer text.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「摘要」，较长文本要点的简短叙述。

entries.definition: To take a part out of a whole, or the part taken.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「提取」或「提取物」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin 'drawn away' image and the common study phrases; the abstract hooks picture a line pulled out of a picture.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁语「抽走」意象与常见学术搭配；抽象记忆点想象从图画中抽出一根线。

normal.en: Abstract is Latin 'drawn away': trahere means to pull.
normal.cn: abstract 是拉丁语「被抽走」：trahere 意为拉。

normal.en: Abstract art keeps shapes and colours but drops the object.
normal.cn: abstract art 保留形状与色彩，却丢掉物体。

normal.en: In the abstract means away from real cases.
normal.cn: in the abstract 意为脱离真实案例。

normal.en: An abstract of a paper sits at the front and sums it up.
normal.cn: abstract of a paper 放在论文前面，概括全文。

normal.en: Abstract as a verb is stressed on the second syllable.
normal.cn: abstract 作动词时重音在第二个音节。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil tracing one line out of a busy drawing and lifting it away.
abstract.cn: 想象一支铅笔从繁复的图画里描出一根线并把它拿走。

abstract.en: Picture a glass jar with oil floating free of crushed seeds.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃罐里油脂从压碎的种子里浮出来。

abstract.en: Picture three canvases of pure colour with no faces and no trees.
abstract.cn: 想象三幅只有纯色、没有面孔也没有树的画布。

examples.en: Freedom is easier to praise in the abstract than to protect in law.
examples.cn: 自由在抽象层面容易赞美，在法律层面却难以保护。

examples.en: The journal asks for an abstract of no more than two hundred words.
examples.cn: 该期刊要求摘要不超过两百词。

examples.en: Researchers abstracted a compound from the bark.
examples.cn: 研究者从树皮中提取出一种化合物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布斯特拉克特」——把具体东西里的关键一根线抽出来，剩下的都是抽象。

root: 拉丁语 abs-（离开）+ trahere（拉），过去分词 abstractus（被抽走的）；核心义是「从具体整体中抽出要点」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the idea drawn out of things, to theory without cases, to a summary drawn from a text, to physical extraction, to art that keeps only form.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从从事物中抽出的观念，走到脱离案例的理论，再到从文本抽出的摘要，以及实际的提取，最后是只保留形式的艺术。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one essential line pulled out of a concrete thing
core.cn: 核心意象：从具体事物中抽出的一根关键线

branches.en: A quality kept in the mind after the object is set aside.
branches.cn: 物体被搁置后，留在心智里的性质。

branches.en: Discussion that never returns to concrete cases.
branches.cn: 从不回到具体案例的讨论。

branches.en: The essentials pulled out and placed before the full text.
branches.cn: 被抽出并放在全文之前的要点。

branches.en: A substance physically removed from its source.
branches.cn: 从来源中实际移出的物质。

branches.en: Both the idea and the summary are things drawn out of a larger whole.
branches.cn: 观念与摘要都是从更大整体中抽出的东西。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin prefix abs- with the pulling root trah-, and its family adds the noun, adverb, and participle endings.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 abs- 与「拉」词根 trah- 结合，其词族再加名词、副词与分词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin abstrahere and its participle abstractus are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record both the verb and the participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abstrahere 及其分词 abstractus 是直接祖先，因此拉丁条目同时记录动词与分词。

definition_zh: 抽象；抽象概念；抽象艺术；心不在焉
definition_en: the act of taking a general idea out of concrete things, such an idea itself, abstract art, or a state of being lost in thought
core_image: 从一堆具体事例里抬起眼睛，只握住共同的那一点
scene: 讨论会上，大家还在争论具体案例，主持人却在白板上写下一条适用于所有案例的规律。The debate moved from cases to a level of abstraction.
sceneCN: 这里 abstraction 是「抽象化、抽象层次」（第 1 个义项：从具体事物中抽出共同观念的过程）；句意为讨论从具体案例转向抽象层面。

pos.zh: 抽象；抽象概念；抽象艺术；心不在焉

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根形式，义为「抽象的」，也可作动词「提取」

由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「心不在焉的」

senses.title: The act of drawing out a general idea
senses.definition: the process of separating a general quality or idea from particular examples
senses.definitionCN: 把共同的性质或观念从具体实例中分离出来的过程
senses.example: Good teaching moves slowly from examples to abstraction.
senses.exampleCN: 好的教学从例子慢慢走向抽象。
senses.why: The suffix -tion names an action, so abstraction first means the mental act of pulling a common feature out of many cases.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -tion 表示动作，因此 abstraction 首先指从众多案例中抽出共同特征的心智活动。

senses.title: A general idea so obtained
senses.definition: a general concept considered apart from the things that show it
senses.definitionCN: 脱离体现它的具体事物而被考虑的一般概念
senses.example: Truth and beauty are abstractions until a person meets them.
senses.exampleCN: 在有人亲身遇见之前，真与美都只是抽象概念。
senses.why: Once the act is finished, the result stands on its own, so the noun shifts from the process to the idea produced.
senses.whyCN: 动作完成后结果独立存在，于是名词从过程转向所产生的观念。

senses.title: Abstract art
senses.definition: art that represent forms and colours rather than recognizable objects
senses.definitionCN: 表现形式与色彩、而非可辨认物象的艺术
senses.example: The museum devoted a whole wing to geometric abstraction.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把整整一翼用于几何抽象艺术。
senses.why: Painting that removes the object until only shape remains repeats the same withdrawal, so the style takes the noun too.
senses.whyCN: 绘画把物体移除到只剩形状，重复了同一种抽离，于是这种风格也使用该名词。

senses.title: Absent-mindedness
senses.definition: a state of being so deep in thought that one ignores surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 沉思到忽略周围环境的状态
senses.example: He stared at the kettle, lost in abstraction.
senses.exampleCN: 他盯着水壶，完全出了神。
senses.why: A mind drawn away from the present scene repeats the literal Latin image, and the word came to name that mental absence.
senses.whyCN: 心智从当前场景被抽走，重复了拉丁语字面意象，这个词便用来指那种心神不在的状态。

intro.en: Abstraction adds the Latin action ending to the same stem as abstract, so its history follows the verb's.
intro.cn: abstraction 在 abstract 的同一词干上加了拉丁语动作后缀，其历史跟随那个动词。

items.en: trahere meant 'to draw or pull' and supplied the root of the family.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖」，提供了这个词族的词根。

items.en: The verb abstrahere meant 'to draw away'.
items.cn: 动词 abstrahere 意为「抽走」。

items.en: abstractio named the act of drawing away, formed with the -tio ending.
items.cn: abstractio 指抽走的动作，由 -tio 后缀构成。

items.en: Old French abstraction carried the learned noun into medieval use.
items.cn: 古法语 abstraction 把这个学术名词带入中世纪用法。

items.en: English abstraction first meant a quality considered apart from its subject.
items.cn: 英语 abstraction 最初指脱离主体而被考虑的性质。

items.en: Modern usage adds abstract art and the everyday phrase lost in abstraction.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了抽象艺术，以及日常短语「出神」。

note.en: The first group gathers forms of the same Latin family; the second gathers words for generality, summary, and daydreaming.
note.cn: 第一组收同一拉丁词族的各种形式；第二组收表示概括、摘要与走神的词。

entries.definition: The adjective and verb from which the noun is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词与动词形式，名词即由它构成。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning deep in thought and unaware of surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「心不在焉的、出神的」。

entries.definition: A pulling toward, from the same Latin trahere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吸引」，同出拉丁语 trahere。

entries.definition: A broad statement drawn from particular cases.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「概括」，由具体案例得出的一般陈述。

entries.definition: A general idea formed in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「概念」，在头脑中形成的一般观念。

entries.definition: An organized set of ideas explaining something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「理论」，解释事物的系统观念。

entries.definition: A pleasant train of thought while awake and distracted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「白日梦」，清醒却分神时的愉快思绪。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -tion pattern and the art sense; the abstract hooks picture a mind stepping up from cases to a rule.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 -tion 构词规律与艺术义；抽象记忆点想象心智从案例走上一条规律。

normal.en: Abstraction is the -tion noun of abstract, so it names the act or the result.
normal.cn: abstraction 是 abstract 的 -tion 名词，指动作或结果。

normal.en: A level of abstraction is the standard phrase in academic writing.
normal.cn: a level of abstraction 是学术写作中的标准短语。

normal.en: Geometric abstraction names art built from pure shapes.
normal.cn: geometric abstraction 指由纯形状构成的艺术。

normal.en: Lost in abstraction describes someone staring away from the room.
normal.cn: lost in abstraction 形容一个人盯着远处、不在现场。

normal.en: Abstract art and the abstract idea share one history of removal.
normal.cn: 抽象艺术与抽象观念共享同一段「抽离」的历史。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifting one clean line out of a crowded drawing.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从拥挤的图画里提起一根干净的线。

abstract.en: Picture a whiteboard rule written after the examples are erased.
abstract.cn: 想象例子被擦掉后白板上留下的一条规律。

abstract.en: Picture a man at a kettle, eyes fixed on nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人守着水壶，眼神落在空处。

examples.en: The course teaches abstraction step by step from real data.
examples.cn: 这门课从真实数据出发，一步步教抽象。

examples.en: Equality is an abstraction that laws must make concrete.
examples.cn: 平等是个抽象概念，必须由法律使之具体。

examples.en: Her abstraction in meetings often hides a sharp mind.
examples.cn: 她在会上出神，往往掩着一个敏锐的头脑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布斯特拉克申」——把具体案例擦掉，白板上剩下的那条规律就叫抽象。

sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从抽出的动作，走到得到的观念，再到丢掉物体的艺术，最后是心神离开现场的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mind stepping up from cases to one shared rule
core.cn: 核心意象：心智从具体案例登上一级共同的规律

branches.en: The mental act of separating a shared feature.
branches.cn: 分离出共同特征的心智动作。

branches.en: The general idea that remains after the act.
branches.cn: 动作之后留下的一般观念。

branches.en: Art that keeps form and drops the recognizable object.
branches.cn: 保留形式、丢掉可辨认物体的艺术。

branches.en: A mind pulled away from the present scene.
branches.cn: 被抽离当下场景的心神。

branches.en: The process and its product share one noun.
branches.cn: 过程与产物共用同一个名词。

intro.en: The noun is built from the same Latin pulling stem, with the action ending -tion and a family of adjective and adverb forms.
intro.cn: 这个名词由同一拉丁「拉」词干加动作后缀 -tion 构成，并带一串形容词与副词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin abstractio is the direct ancestor, formed from abstrahere with the action suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abstractio 是直接祖先，由 abstrahere 加动作后缀构成。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「抽象的」

definition_zh: 荒谬的；荒唐可笑的；荒诞（哲学概念）
definition_en: so unreasonable or ill-matched that it seems ridiculous, or the idea that human life lacks inherent meaning
core_image: 一个人认真排队，却排在一个根本没有门的墙前
scene: 剧场里，演员一本正经地讨论如何用一把没有底的桶运水，观众先愣住，随后大笑。The plan sounded absurd until everyone laughed.
sceneCN: 这里 absurd 是「荒谬可笑的」（第 1 个义项：完全不合常理，因而显得可笑）；句意为这个计划听起来荒谬，直到众人都笑了。

collocations.zh: 把某事推到荒唐的地步

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「荒谬；荒谬之事」
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「荒谬地；离谱地」
由本词加主义后缀构成，义为「荒诞主义」

senses.title: Wildly unreasonable
senses.definition: so contrary to reason or common sense that it cannot be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 与理性或常识相违到无法接受的程度
senses.example: It is absurd to expect a reply within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 指望一小时内得到回复是荒谬的。
senses.why: Latin absurdus meant 'out of tune', a sound that clashes; a claim that clashes with reason is heard as jarring, hence absurd.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absurdus 意为「不合调」，指刺耳走调的声音；与理性不合调的说法听起来同样刺耳，于是成为荒谬。

senses.title: Laughably ill-matched
senses.definition: so badly matched to its setting that the mismatch becomes comic
senses.definitionCN: 与情境严重不匹配，以致错位本身变得滑稽
senses.example: He wore a winter coat on the hottest day, an absurd sight.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最热的一天穿冬大衣，样子荒唐可笑。
senses.why: When the clash is visible rather than merely argued, the word slides from 'illogical' to 'funny in its wrongness'.
senses.whyCN: 当这种冲突被看见而不只是被论证，词义就从「不合逻辑」滑向「错得可笑」。

senses.title: The absurd as a philosophy
senses.definition: the idea that human beings seek meaning in a universe that offers none
senses.definitionCN: 认为人在一个不提供意义的宇宙中寻求意义的观念
senses.example: Camus wrote about the absurd as a meeting of human longing and silent world.
senses.exampleCN: 加缪把荒诞写成人间渴望与沉默世界的相遇。
senses.why: Twentieth-century writers turned the everyday adjective into a noun for the human condition, where reason demands meaning and the world stays mute.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪作家把这个日常形容词转为指人类处境的名称：理性要求意义，世界却保持沉默。

intro.en: Absurd began as a musical word: Latin absurdus described something out of tune, and the clash of sound became a clash of sense.
intro.cn: absurd 最初是音乐用语：拉丁语 absurdus 指走调之物，声音的冲突延伸为意义的冲突。

items.en: surdus meant 'deaf, dull, muffled', and it also gave the mathematical word surd.
items.cn: surdus 意为「聋的、沉闷的」，也衍生出数学词 surd。

items.en: absurdus meant 'out of tune, harsh-sounding', built with the prefix ab-.
items.cn: absurdus 意为「走调的、刺耳的」，由前缀 ab- 构成。

items.en: The neuter absurdum named something discordant or senseless.
items.cn: 中性形式 absurdum 指不和谐或无意义之物。

items.en: French absurde narrowed the meaning to 'contrary to reason'.
items.cn: 法语 absurde 把词义收窄为「违背理性」。

items.en: English absurd first meant musically harsh, then plainly unreasonable.
items.cn: 英语 absurd 先指音乐上刺耳，后指明显不合理。

items.en: The twentieth century added the noun phrase the absurd for a philosophical stance.
items.cn: 二十世纪增加了名词短语 the absurd，用于哲学立场。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adverb, and movement word from the same family; the second gathers words for what defies reason.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的名称、副词与主义词；第二组收表示违背理性的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being absurd, or an absurd act.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荒谬」或「荒谬之事」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in a ridiculous degree'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「荒谬地、离谱地」。

entries.definition: A literary and philosophical movement built on the absurd.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荒诞主义」，以荒诞为基础的文学与哲学思潮。

entries.definition: A mathematics term for an irrational root, from the same Latin surdus.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，数学术语「无理根」，同出拉丁语 surdus。

entries.definition: An adjective for something that invites laughter by being unreasonable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可笑的」，因不合理而招人发笑。

entries.definition: An adjective for something utterly contrary to nature or sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒唐的」，完全违背常理。

entries.definition: An adjective for something so foolish that it is comic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「滑稽荒唐的」，愚蠢到好笑。

entries.definition: An adjective for statements that carry no sensible meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无意义的、荒谬的」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'out of tune' origin and the common degree phrases; the abstract hooks picture a plan clashing with reality like a wrong note.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「走调」来源与常见程度搭配；抽象记忆点想象计划像错音一样与现实不合调。

normal.en: Absurd came from a word for 'out of tune': a claim can clash like a wrong note.
normal.cn: absurd 来自「走调」一词：一个说法可以像错音一样刺耳。

normal.en: An absurd idea and an absurdly cheap price are the everyday patterns.
normal.cn: an absurd idea 与 absurdly cheap 是日常搭配。

normal.en: The noun is absurdity, and the adverb is absurdly.
normal.cn: 名词是 absurdity，副词是 absurdly。

normal.en: Theatre of the absurd names plays that refuse ordinary logic.
normal.cn: theatre of the absurd 指拒绝常规逻辑的戏剧。

normal.en: In philosophy the absurd names the clash between human meaning and a silent world.
normal.cn: 哲学中 the absurd 指人类求意义与沉默世界之间的冲突。

abstract.en: Picture a queue of people waiting patiently before a wall with no door.
abstract.cn: 想象一队人耐心地排在一堵没有门的墙前。

abstract.en: Picture a musician playing one loud wrong note in a quiet hall.
abstract.cn: 想象乐手在安静的音乐厅里弹出一个响亮的错音。

abstract.en: Picture a man carrying water in a bucket with no bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人用没有底的桶运水。

examples.en: It is absurd to blame the weather for a bad decision.
examples.cn: 把糟糕的决定归咎于天气是荒谬的。

examples.en: The meeting ended in an absurd argument about chairs.
examples.cn: 会议以一场关于椅子的荒唐争吵收场。

examples.en: Camus made the absurd central to his essays.
examples.cn: 加缪把荒诞置于其随笔的核心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布瑟德」——声音走调刺耳，道理走调就成了荒谬。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（偏离）+ surdus（聋的、沉闷的）→ absurdus（走调的）；核心义是「与常理不合调」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a claim that clashes with reason, to a mismatch that makes people laugh, to the philosophical name for a meaningless universe.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从与理性冲突的说法，走到引人发笑的错位，再到哲学上对无意义宇宙的命名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a note that clashes with the music around it
core.cn: 核心意象：一个与周围音乐不合的音

branches.en: A claim that clashes with reason the way a wrong note clashes with music.
branches.cn: 与理性冲突的说法，如同错音与音乐冲突。

branches.en: A mismatch that stands in plain sight and turns comic.
branches.cn: 摆在眼前的错位，转为滑稽。

branches.en: A philosophy naming the silence of the universe before human longing.
branches.cn: 一种哲学，命名宇宙在人类渴望面前的沉默。

branches.en: Both the everyday and the philosophical sense rest on a clash that cannot be resolved.
branches.cn: 日常义与哲学义都建立在无法化解的冲突上。

branches.en: The comic clash and the cosmic clash share the same mismatch.
branches.cn: 滑稽的错位与宇宙的错位共享同一种不匹配。

intro.en: The word keeps a Latin prefix and a deafness root, and its family grows with the noun, adverb, and movement endings -ity, -ly, and -ism.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语前缀与「聋」词根构成，其词族以后缀 -ity、-ly、-ism 生长。

latinIntro.en: Latin absurdus is the direct ancestor, and surdus is the root that also gave the mathematical term.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 absurdus 是直接祖先，surdus 是同时也衍生数学术语的词根。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「荒谬；荒谬之事」
名词，义为「荒诞主义」

definition_zh: 丰富；大量；充裕；生态多度
definition_en: a large quantity of something, great plenty, or the number of a species in a given area
core_image: 谷仓里的麦子堆到屋顶，门都关不上
scene: 秋收后粮仓装满了，麻袋一直堆到门口，主人笑着说今年不用愁。There was an abundance of grain after the harvest.
sceneCN: 这里 abundance 是「丰富、大量」（第 1 个义项：数量远超所需）；句意为秋收后粮食十分充裕。

derivatives.zh: 由本词同源词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「丰富的、大量的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「大量地、十分清楚地」

senses.title: A great quantity
senses.definition: a very large amount of something, more than enough
senses.definitionCN: 某物的极大数量，多到超过所需
senses.example: The river valley offers an abundance of fresh water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个河谷提供大量淡水。
senses.why: Latin abundare meant 'to overflow'; abundance pictures a supply that runs over the brim instead of running short.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abundare 意为「溢出」；abundance 描绘的是漫过边缘而不是即将见底的供应。

senses.title: Wealth and plenty
senses.definition: a condition of comfortable wealth or plentiful resources
senses.definitionCN: 舒适的富裕状态或资源充足的状态
senses.example: They lived in abundance after the shop prospered.
senses.exampleCN: 店铺兴旺之后，他们过上了富足的生活。
senses.why: When overflowing supply persists, it becomes a way of life rather than one full barn, so the word names prosperity itself.
senses.whyCN: 当溢出的供应持续存在，它就不只是一座满仓，而成为生活方式，于是这个词指富裕本身。

senses.title: A count of organisms
senses.definition: the number of individuals of a species in a defined area
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种在界定区域内的个体数量
senses.example: Ecologists measured the abundance of beetles in each plot.
senses.exampleCN: 生态学家测量了每个样地里甲虫的多度。
senses.why: Field science needs a neutral count word, and it borrows the plain noun for plentiful numbers without implying any judgement.
senses.whyCN: 野外科学需要一个中性的计数词，于是借用了这个朴素名词，表示数量多而不带价值判断。

intro.en: Abundance comes from Latin abundare, 'to overflow', a river image applied to supplies.
intro.cn: abundance 来自拉丁语 abundare（溢出），是把河流意象用在物资上。

items.en: unda meant 'wave', and it survives in undulate.
items.cn: unda 意为「波浪」，仍见于 undulate。

items.en: The prefix ab- here intensifies rather than separates, giving 'away, over'.
items.cn: 这里的前缀 ab- 起加强作用而非分离，意为「向外、过度」。

items.en: abundare meant 'to overflow, run over like water'.
items.cn: abundare 意为「溢出」，像水一样漫过。

items.en: abundantia named the state of overflowing plenty.
items.cn: abundantia 指溢出般充裕的状态。

items.en: Old French passed abundance to English with the sense of great plenty.
items.cn: 古法语把 abundance 传给英语，义为大量充裕。

items.en: Modern English keeps the everyday sense and adds the ecological count sense.
items.cn: 现代英语保留日常义，并增加生态学的计数义。

note.en: The first group gathers same-family adjectives and adverbs plus a wave word; the second gathers words for large supply.
note.cn: 第一组收同族形容词、副词与一个「波浪」词；第二组收表示大量供应的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning existing in large quantities.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「丰富的、大量的」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in large quantity' or 'very clearly'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「大量地」或「十分清楚地」。

entries.definition: To flood or overwhelm, from the same Latin wave.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「淹没、使不堪应付」，同出拉丁语「波浪」。

entries.definition: To move in waves.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「波动、起伏」。

entries.definition: A large or sufficient amount.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大量、充足」。

entries.definition: An extravagant quantity, often of things growing or spread.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大量、繁盛」，常指生长或铺开之物。

entries.definition: A large amount of money or resources.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「财富」，大量金钱或资源。

entries.definition: A rapid increase in number.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「激增、扩散」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the overflowing river image and the fixed phrases; the abstract hooks picture a granary with grain spilling past the door.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用河流溢出的意象与固定短语；抽象记忆点想象粮仓的粮食溢出门外。

normal.en: Abundance comes from a Latin word for overflow, like a river over its banks.
normal.cn: abundance 来自拉丁语「溢出」，如同河水漫过河堤。

normal.en: An abundance of and in abundance are the two fixed patterns.
normal.cn: an abundance of 与 in abundance 是两个固定结构。

normal.en: The adjective is abundant, the adverb abundantly.
normal.cn: 形容词是 abundant，副词是 abundantly。

normal.en: Abundance of caution is a formal way of saying extreme care.
normal.cn: abundance of caution 是表示「极度谨慎」的正式说法。

normal.en: In ecology, abundance simply counts individuals per area.
normal.cn: 生态学中 abundance 只统计单位面积内的个体数。

abstract.en: Picture a granary so full that sacks block the doorway.
abstract.cn: 想象粮仓满到麻袋堵住门口。

abstract.en: Picture a river rising over its bank into the fields.
abstract.cn: 想象河水上涨漫过河岸流进田里。

abstract.en: Picture a market stall with fruit piled higher than the awning.
abstract.cn: 想象摊位上的水果堆得比遮阳篷还高。

examples.en: There is an abundance of cheap flights in summer.
examples.cn: 夏季有大量廉价航班。

examples.en: Wild mushrooms grow in abundance after rain.
examples.cn: 雨后野蘑菇大量生长。

examples.en: The survey recorded the abundance of fish along the reef.
examples.cn: 这次调查记录了礁石一带鱼类的多度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿班丹斯」——河水漫过河堤，粮食溢出门外，都是「丰富」。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（向外、过度）+ unda（波浪）+ -are → abundare（溢出）；核心义是「多到漫过边缘」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from an overflowing quantity, to a lasting condition of wealth, to a neutral ecological count.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从溢出的数量，走到持久的富足状态，再到中性的生态计数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a supply overflowing its container
core.cn: 核心意象：漫出容器的供应

branches.en: A quantity that runs over the brim.
branches.cn: 漫过边缘的数量。

branches.en: Overflow that becomes a settled way of life.
branches.cn: 溢出成为稳定的生活方式。

branches.en: A neutral count of individuals in an area.
branches.cn: 区域内个体数的中性统计。

branches.en: Both senses rest on numbers that are simply there in quantity.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在数量本身之多的基础上。

branches.en: One full barn becomes a whole prosperous household.
branches.cn: 一座满仓扩展为整个富足的家户。

intro.en: The word joins a Latin prefix of excess with the wave root und-, and its family grows with adjective and adverb endings.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示过度的拉丁语前缀与「波浪」词根 und- 结合，词族以形容词与副词后缀生长。

latinIntro.en: Latin abundare and abundantia are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the verb and the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abundare 与 abundantia 是直接祖先，因此拉丁条目记录动词与名词。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「丰富的；大量的」
副词，义为「大量地；十分清楚地」

definition_zh: 丰富的；大量的；富含……的；过多的
definition_en: existing in large quantities, richly supplied with something, or more than is needed
core_image: 果树枝条被果实压弯，摘都摘不完
scene: 果园里苹果结得压弯了枝，地上还落了一层，主人发愁没人来收。Apples were so abundant that many fell and rotted.
sceneCN: 这里 abundant 是「大量的、丰富的」（第 1 个义项：数量极多）；句意为苹果多到许多掉在地上腐烂。

derivatives.zh: 由本词同源词干加名词后缀构成，义为「丰富；大量」
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「大量地；十分清楚地」

senses.title: Existing in large amounts
senses.definition: present in great quantity, far beyond a bare minimum
senses.definitionCN: 以极大数量存在，远超最低所需
senses.example: Fish were abundant in the lake before the dam was built.
senses.exampleCN: 建坝之前，这个湖里鱼非常多。
senses.why: The adjective comes from a verb meaning 'to overflow', so abundant describes a supply that spills past the container rather than barely filling it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词来自意为「溢出」的动词，因此 abundant 形容供应漫出容器，而不是勉强装满。

senses.title: Richly supplied with something
senses.definition: containing a particular element or quality in large measure
senses.definitionCN: 含有某种成分或品质的量很大
senses.example: The region is abundant in copper and timber.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区富含铜矿与木材。
senses.why: With the preposition in, the adjective points to what overflows inside a place, turning plenty into a description of composition.
senses.whyCN: 与介词 in 连用时，这个形容词指向某地内部溢出的是什么，把「多」转为对成分的描述。

senses.title: More than necessary
senses.definition: so plentiful as to be excessive or wasteful
senses.definitionCN: 多到成为过剩或浪费的程度
senses.example: The report is abundant in detail but short on argument.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告细节过多，论证却不足。
senses.why: An overflowing supply can drown what matters, so the same word sometimes criticizes excess rather than praising plenty.
senses.whyCN: 溢出的供应可能淹没重点，因此同一个词有时批评过剩而非称赞充足。

intro.en: Abundant is the adjective from Latin abundare, 'to overflow', the same source as abundance.
intro.cn: abundant 是拉丁语 abundare（溢出）的形容词，与 abundance 同源。

items.en: unda meant 'wave', a root also seen in undulate.
items.cn: unda 意为「波浪」，也见于 undulate。

items.en: abundare meant 'to overflow, run over'.
items.cn: abundare 意为「溢出、漫过」。

items.en: The present participle abundans meant 'overflowing' and became the adjective stem.
items.cn: 现在分词 abundans 意为「正在溢出」，成为形容词词干。

items.en: Old French abundant kept the sense of great plenty.
items.cn: 古法语 abundant 保留了大量充裕义。

items.en: English abundant first described copious supply and later rich content.
items.cn: 英语 abundant 先描述供应充沛，后描述内容丰富。

items.en: Modern usage fixes the pattern abundant in for a place full of something.
items.cn: 现代用法固定了 abundant in 这一结构，指某地充满某物。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adverb, and root verb; the second gathers adjectives for large supply.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、副词与同源动词；第二组收表示大量供应的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning a great quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「丰富、大量」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in large quantity'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「大量地」。

entries.definition: The Latin verb 'to overflow' that begins the family.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语动词，义为「溢出」，为这个词族的起点。

entries.definition: An adjective for a supply that is more than enough.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充足的」，供应绰绰有余。

entries.definition: An adjective for large amounts, often of writing or notes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「大量的」，常用于文字或笔记。

entries.definition: An adjective for something given or produced in extravagant amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「大量的、挥霍般的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for enough or more than enough space or supply.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充足的」，空间或供应足够有余。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the overflowing root and the fixed preposition pattern; the abstract hooks picture branches bent under too much fruit.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「溢出」词根与固定介词结构；抽象记忆点想象枝条被果实压弯。

normal.en: Abundant shares the Latin overflow root with abundance.
normal.cn: abundant 与 abundance 共享拉丁语「溢出」词根。

normal.en: Abundant in means full of a particular thing.
normal.cn: abundant in 意为富含某种东西。

normal.en: Abundant evidence and abundant resources are common academic phrases.
normal.cn: abundant evidence 与 abundant resources 是常见学术搭配。

normal.en: The adverb abundantly often means 'very clearly', as in abundantly clear.
normal.cn: 副词 abundantly 常表示「十分清楚」，如 abundantly clear。

normal.en: Unlike plentiful, abundant can also criticize wasteful excess.
normal.cn: 与 plentiful 不同，abundant 也可批评浪费性的过剩。

abstract.en: Picture branches bent to the ground under apples.
abstract.cn: 想象枝条被苹果压到地面。

abstract.en: Picture a warehouse where boxes block the aisles.
abstract.cn: 想象仓库里的箱子堵住了走道。

abstract.en: Picture a report padded with detail until the point vanishes.
abstract.cn: 想象报告堆满细节，重点反而消失。

examples.en: Water is abundant in the wet season and scarce in the dry.
examples.cn: 雨季水多，旱季水少。

examples.en: The soil here is abundant in nitrogen.
examples.cn: 这里的土壤富含氮。

examples.en: The essay offers abundant quotations but little analysis.
examples.cn: 这篇文章引文很多，分析却很少。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from sheer quantity, to a place full of a substance, to a quantity so large it becomes excess.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从纯粹的数量多，走到某处充满某种成分，再到多到成为过剩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fruit bending the branches under its weight
core.cn: 核心意象：果实把枝条压弯的重量

branches.en: A supply that overflows the ordinary measure.
branches.cn: 漫出常规尺度的供应。

branches.en: A place whose contents overflow with one substance.
branches.cn: 内部充满某种物质的场所。

branches.en: Overflow that turns into wasteful excess.
branches.cn: 溢出转为浪费性的过剩。

branches.en: The quantity and the composition senses share one image of overflow.
branches.cn: 数量义与成分义共享同一个溢出意象。

branches.en: Being full of one thing can crowd out the rest.
branches.cn: 被一种东西充满，可能挤掉其余。

latinIntro.en: Latin abundans is the direct ancestor, formed from the verb abundare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abundans 是直接祖先，由动词 abundare 构成。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「丰富；大量」
副词，义为「大量地；十分清楚地」

definition_zh: 滥用；虐待；辱骂；滥用行为
definition_en: to use something wrongly or too much, to treat a person or animal cruelly, or to speak to someone insultingly
core_image: 一件本该正当使用的工具被反复乱用，直到损坏
scene: 图书馆管理员发现有人把公共打印机当作私人复印机，一天印了几百页，纸都被用光。Staff reported the abuse of the printing service.
sceneCN: 这里 abuse 是「滥用」（第 1 个义项：不正当或过度使用）；句意为员工举报了打印服务的滥用。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「辱骂的；虐待的」
由本词加施动者后缀构成，义为「施虐者；滥用者」

senses.title: To use something wrongly or excessively
senses.definition: to make wrong or excessive use of a thing, a right, or a power
senses.definitionCN: 错误或过度地使用某物、某项权利或权力
senses.example: He abused his access to the files to read private records.
senses.exampleCN: 他滥用文件访问权限，查看了私人记录。
senses.why: Latin abuti meant 'to use up wrongly'; the prefix turns ordinary use into use that wastes or misdirects the thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abuti 意为「错误地用尽」；前缀把正常使用变成浪费或误导性的使用。

senses.title: Wrong or excessive use as a noun
senses.definition: the act or practice of using something wrongly or too much
senses.definitionCN: 错误或过度使用某物的行为或做法
senses.example: The report documents the abuse of public funds.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了公共资金的滥用。
senses.why: Once the verb names the act, the noun names the act itself, and compounds such as drug abuse fix it in policy language.
senses.whyCN: 动词命名动作后，名词就指这一行为本身，drug abuse 这类复合词把它固定在政策语言中。

senses.title: Cruel treatment of a person or animal
senses.definition: the repeated mistreatment of a person or animal, causing harm
senses.definitionCN: 对人反复施加、造成伤害的恶劣对待
senses.example: The shelter rescues dogs that have suffered abuse.
senses.exampleCN: 这家收容所救助遭受虐待的狗。
senses.why: Using a living creature as if it were a tool to break is a misuse of a body, so the word extends from objects and powers to people and animals.
senses.whyCN: 把活物当作可损坏的工具，是对身体的误用，于是词义从物品与权力扩展到人与动物。

senses.title: Insulting language
senses.definition: rude and insulting speech directed at someone
senses.definitionCN: 针对某人的粗鲁侮辱性言语
senses.example: The referee reported abuse from the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判报告了观众席上的辱骂。
senses.why: Speech itself can be misused: words thrown to injure rather than to communicate, so verbal abuse joins the same family.
senses.whyCN: 言语本身也会被误用：词语不是用来沟通而是用来伤人，于是 verbal abuse 归入同一族。

intro.en: Abuse comes from Latin abuti, 'to use up wrongly', where the prefix ab- turns usus, 'use', into misuse.
intro.cn: abuse 来自拉丁语 abuti（错误地用尽），前缀 ab- 把 usus（使用）变成误用。

items.en: uti meant 'to use', and it gave usus and the English word use.
items.cn: uti 意为「使用」，衍生出 usus 与英语 use。

items.en: abuti meant 'to use up, misuse', with ab- marking deviation.
items.cn: abuti 意为「用尽、误用」，ab- 表示偏离。

items.en: abusus meant 'misuse', and the noun passed through French.
items.cn: abusus 意为「误用」，该名词经法语传入。

items.en: Old French abus named a wrong use or a deception.
items.cn: 古法语 abus 指错误使用或欺骗。

items.en: English abuse first meant misuse, then extended to mistreatment and insults.
items.cn: 英语 abuse 先指误用，后扩展到虐待与辱骂。

items.en: Modern policy language fixes compounds such as drug abuse and abuse of power.
items.cn: 现代政策语言固定了 drug abuse 与 abuse of power 等复合说法。

note.en: The first group gathers the adjective, the agent noun, and the verb root; the second gathers words for harm and insult.
note.cn: 第一组收形容词、施动者名词与同源动词；第二组收表示伤害与侮辱的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning insulting or harmfully used.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「辱骂的、虐待的」。

entries.definition: A person who mistreats others or misuses something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「施虐者、滥用者」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to touch or border on, with a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「毗邻」，词根不同。

entries.definition: A noun or verb for wrong use, without the cruelty sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「误用」，不含虐待义。

entries.definition: A noun for bad or unfair treatment of a person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「虐待、不公对待」。

entries.definition: A noun or verb for a rude remark that offends.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「侮辱」。

entries.definition: A noun for unfair use of people or resources for gain.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剥削、开发利用」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin 'use up wrongly' origin and the fixed compounds; the abstract hooks picture a shared tool ruined by careless hands.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁语「误用」来源与固定复合词；抽象记忆点想象公用的工具被乱用弄坏。

normal.en: Abuse is literally 'wrong use': ab- away plus usus use.
normal.cn: abuse 字面是「错误使用」：ab- 偏离加 usus 使用。

normal.en: Noun stress is on the second syllable, and the verb ends with a z sound.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第二音节，动词结尾读 z 音。

normal.en: Drug abuse and abuse of power are the most frequent compounds.
normal.cn: drug abuse 与 abuse of power 是最常见的复合说法。

normal.en: The adjective abusive describes both words and behaviour.
normal.cn: 形容词 abusive 既可描述言语，也可描述行为。

normal.en: The same word covers tools, powers, bodies, and speech.
normal.cn: 同一个词覆盖工具、权力、身体与言语。

abstract.en: Picture a public printer churning out pages until the paper runs out.
abstract.cn: 想象公用打印机一直印到纸用光。

abstract.en: Picture a key meant for one door being tried on every lock.
abstract.cn: 想象一把本该开一扇门的钥匙被拿去试遍所有锁。

abstract.en: Picture a voice raised only to wound, never to explain.
abstract.cn: 想象一个只为伤人、从不解释的声音。

examples.en: Managers who abuse their authority lose public trust.
examples.cn: 滥用职权的管理者会失去公众信任。

examples.en: The charity was accused of the abuse of donated funds.
examples.cn: 该慈善机构被指控滥用捐款。

examples.en: The law protects animals from abuse.
examples.cn: 法律保护动物免受虐待。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿比尤斯」——一把好用的工具被乱用到坏，就是滥用。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（偏离）+ uti（使用）→ abuti（误用）→ abusus；核心义是「把用途用偏、用坏」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from misusing a thing, to the act named as a noun, to mistreating a body, to words thrown as weapons.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从误用某物，走到以名词命名的行为，再到虐待身体，最后是把言语当作武器投出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shared tool ruined by careless, wrong use
core.cn: 核心意象：被错误乱用而损坏的公用工具

branches.en: A right or a tool turned to the wrong purpose.
branches.cn: 被转向错误用途的权利或工具。

branches.en: The act itself, named in policy and reports.
branches.cn: 行为本身，在政策与报告中命名。

branches.en: A living body treated as a thing to break.
branches.cn: 被当作可损坏之物的活体。

branches.en: Speech used to injure instead of to communicate.
branches.cn: 言语被用来伤人而非沟通。

branches.en: Misuse of a power and misuse of speech both bend a gift away from its purpose.
branches.cn: 滥用权力与滥用言语都把天赋之物扭离本来的用途。

intro.en: The word pairs the Latin prefix ab- with the use root ut-, and its family adds adjective and agent endings.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 ab- 与「使用」词根 ut- 结合，词族另加形容词与施动者后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin abuti and abusus are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the verb and the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abuti 与 abusus 是直接祖先，因此拉丁条目记录动词与名词。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「辱骂的；虐待的」
名词，义为「施虐者；滥用者」

definition_zh: 毗邻；紧靠；与……接界
definition_en: to touch or border on something along an edge
core_image: 两堵墙的边线贴在一起，中间没有缝隙
scene: 测绘员沿地界走了一圈，指着篱笆说，这块地正好贴着后面的林地。Their garden abuts the edge of the forest.
sceneCN: 这里 abut 是「毗邻、接界」（第 1 个义项：土地沿边界相接）；句意为他们的花园紧贴着森林边缘。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「桥台；支承结构」
由动词加现在分词后缀构成，义为「紧邻的、毗连的」

senses.title: To border on land
senses.definition: of land or a building, to touch another property along a boundary
senses.definitionCN: 指土地或建筑沿边界与另一处相接
senses.example: Their farm abuts the nature reserve on the north side.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的农场北侧紧靠自然保护区。
senses.why: Middle English abuten came from a word meaning 'to end at', so the verb marks where one property ends against another.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 abuten 来自意为「止于」的词，因此这个动词标记一块地产止于另一块的位置。

senses.title: To meet and bear against
senses.definition: of structural parts, to meet and support one another
senses.definitionCN: 指结构部件相互接触并承托
senses.example: The arch abuts the stone piers on both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 拱体抵住两侧的石墩。
senses.why: Builders speak of one part abutting another when two edges meet under load, which is why the supporting block is called an abutment.
senses.whyCN: 建筑者用「一部分抵住另一部分」描述两边在受力下相接，因此承托的砌块被称为 abutment（桥台）。

intro.en: Abut comes from Middle English abuten, 'to end at or border on', and survives mainly in property and building descriptions.
intro.cn: abut 来自中古英语 abuten（止于、接界），现今主要用于地产与建筑描写。

items.en: bouter meant 'to push, thrust', from a Germanic source.
items.cn: bouter 意为「推、顶」，源自日耳曼语。

items.en: abuten combined a prefix with bouter and meant 'to end at'.
items.cn: abuten 由前缀与 bouter 结合，意为「止于」。

items.en: Property law adopted abut for land that touches another holding.
items.cn: 财产法采用 abut 指与另一块地产相接的土地。

items.en: Builders used abut for parts that meet and carry load.
items.cn: 建筑用语用 abut 指相接并承重的部件。

items.en: The noun abutment named the masonry that receives the thrust of an arch.
items.cn: 名词 abutment 指承受拱推力的砌体。

items.en: Modern usage keeps the verb in surveying, planning, and structural writing.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个动词保留在测量、规划与结构写作中。

note.en: The first group gathers forms of the same small family; the second gathers verbs for neighbouring and touching.
note.cn: 第一组收同一小词族的各种形式；第二组收表示相邻与接触的动词。

entries.definition: The supporting structure at the end of a bridge or arch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「桥台」，桥或拱端的承托结构。

entries.definition: The participle used as an adjective for adjoining property.
entries.definitionCN: 分词作形容词，义为「紧邻的」。

entries.definition: The past tense, common in surveys of boundaries.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式，常用于边界测量。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to lie next to a boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「与……接界」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to be next to or joined with.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「毗连、邻接」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to come into contact with.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接触」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to be situated next to.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「邻近」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the surveying image and the fixed prepositions; the abstract hooks picture two boundary lines pressed together.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用测量意象与固定介词；抽象记忆点想象两条边界线压在一起。

normal.en: Abut is mostly a property word: land abuts land.
normal.cn: abut 主要是地产用词：土地紧邻土地。

normal.en: The usual prepositions are on and against.
normal.cn: 常用介词是 on 与 against。

normal.en: The noun abutment names the block that takes an arch's push.
normal.cn: 名词 abutment 指承受拱推力的砌块。

normal.en: The double t stays doubled before -ed and -ing.
normal.cn: 加 -ed 与 -ing 时双写 t。

normal.en: Adjoin is the more common synonym in general writing.
normal.cn: 在一般写作中 adjoin 是更常见的同义词。

abstract.en: Picture two garden fences sharing one line with no gap.
abstract.cn: 想象两道篱笆共用一条线，中间没有缝隙。

abstract.en: Picture an arch pressing its weight into stone piers.
abstract.cn: 想象拱把重量压进石墩。

abstract.en: Picture a surveyor walking the edge where field meets forest.
abstract.cn: 想象测量员走在田野与森林相接的边上。

examples.en: The warehouse abuts the railway line.
examples.cn: 仓库紧靠铁路线。

examples.en: Rooms abutting the courtyard have no outside windows.
examples.cn: 紧邻庭院的房间没有外窗。

examples.en: The new road will abut the western boundary of the site.
examples.cn: 新路将紧贴场地的西侧边界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿巴特」——两块地的边线贴在一起，谁也不留缝，就是毗邻。

root: 古法语 bouter（推、顶）→ 中古英语 abuten（止于）；核心义是「边界抵到另一处」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from land that ends against other land, to structural parts that meet under load.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从止于另一块土地的地产，走到在受力下相接的结构部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two edges pressed together without a gap
core.cn: 核心意象：两条边压在一起，没有缝隙

branches.en: One property ending where another begins.
branches.cn: 一块地产止于另一块开始处。

branches.en: Building parts that meet and carry thrust.
branches.cn: 相接并承受推力的建筑部件。

branches.en: In both senses one edge stops against another.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是一条边抵在另一条边上。

branches.en: The bridge abutment is the built form of the same meeting.
branches.cn: 桥台是这种相接的建筑形态。

branches.en: Surveying and masonry share one verb of contact.
branches.cn: 测量与砌筑共用同一个表示接触的动词。

intro.en: The word is short and mostly indivisible; its family grows with the agent noun abutment and the participial adjective abutting.
intro.cn: 这个词很短且基本不可再分；词族以名词 abutment 与分词形容词 abutting 生长。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; the word came through Old French from a Germanic pushing verb, so the Latin entries are left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语祖先；该词经古法语来自日耳曼语表示「推」的动词，因此拉丁条目留空。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「桥台；支承结构」
形容词，义为「紧邻的、毗连的」

definition_zh: 学术界；学术圈；学术生活
definition_en: the world of universities, colleges, and research, or the professional life of scholars
core_image: 一圈讲堂、图书馆与实验室围成的独立世界
scene: 年轻研究者犹豫要不要离开大学去企业工作，导师说留在学术圈意味着自由，也意味着长期清贫。She chose to stay in academia despite the lower pay.
sceneCN: 这里 academia 是「学术界」（第 1 个义项：大学与研究机构构成的整体）；句意为她不顾较低薪水，仍选择留在学术界。

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根加形容词后缀构成，义为「学术的；学院的」
由形容词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「院士」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「学术上」

senses.title: The institutions of higher learning
senses.definition: the universities, colleges, and research bodies taken as one world
senses.definitionCN: 把大学、学院与研究机构视为一个整体世界
senses.example: Funding cuts are felt across academia.
senses.exampleCN: 经费削减在整个学术界都能感受到。
senses.why: The word is the Latin name of Plato's school; a single garden became the label for every institution of learning together.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是柏拉图学园的拉丁名称；一座园子后来成了所有学术机构合称的标签。

senses.title: The profession of scholars
senses.definition: the working life, norms, and career path of researchers and teachers
senses.definitionCN: 研究者与教师的工作生活、规范与职业路径
senses.example: She left industry to return to academia.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开产业界，回到学术圈。
senses.why: Once a place name becomes a group name, it can also name a way of working, with its own habits, pressures, and rewards.
senses.whyCN: 当地名变成群体名，它也能指一种工作方式，带着自己的习惯、压力与回报。

intro.en: Academia is the Latin name of the grove where Plato taught, later applied to the scholarly world as a whole.
intro.cn: academia 是柏拉图授课那片园林的拉丁名称，后来指整个学术世界。

items.en: Akademeia was the park outside Athens named after the hero Akademos.
items.cn: Akademeia 是雅典城外以英雄阿卡德摩斯命名的园林。

items.en: Plato taught in that grove, and his school took the name.
items.cn: 柏拉图在那片园林讲学，他的学园因此得名。

items.en: Latin academia named the school and, more broadly, learned study.
items.cn: 拉丁语 academia 指该学园，也泛指学术研究。

items.en: English first borrowed academy for a society of learning.
items.cn: 英语先借入 academy，指学术团体。

items.en: The adjective academic extended the name to university work.
items.cn: 形容词 academic 把这一名称扩展到大学工作。

items.en: Modern English uses academia for the whole scholarly world and its career.
items.cn: 现代英语用 academia 指整个学术世界及其职业。

note.en: The first group gathers adjective and person nouns from the same family; the second gathers words for the scholarly world and its members.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的形容词与人物名词；第二组收表示学术世界及其成员的词。

entries.definition: An adjective for university study, also a noun for a scholar.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「学术的」；也可作名词指「学者」。

entries.definition: A member of a learned academy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「院士」，学术机构的成员。

entries.definition: A learned society or a school.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学院、学会」。

entries.definition: Serious academic study or the funding that supports it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学术研究」或「奖学金」。

entries.definition: Study at university level.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「高等教育」。

entries.definition: The institution or sector as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「大学（系统）」。

entries.definition: Systematic investigation that defines much academic work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「研究」，系统性的探究。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use Plato's grove and the career phrases; the abstract hooks picture a walled garden of lecture halls and libraries.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用柏拉图园林与职业搭配；抽象记忆点想象讲堂与图书馆围成的园子。

normal.en: Academia is the Latin name of Plato's grove, Akademeia.
normal.cn: academia 是柏拉图园林阿卡德米亚的拉丁名称。

normal.en: Stay in academia and leave academia are the two career phrases.
normal.cn: stay in academia 与 leave academia 是两个职业短语。

normal.en: Academia and industry is the standard contrast.
normal.cn: academia and industry 是标准对照。

normal.en: The adjective academic also works as a noun for a scholar.
normal.cn: 形容词 academic 也可作名词指学者。

normal.en: Academia names a world, not a single university.
normal.cn: academia 指一个世界，而不是某一所大学。

abstract.en: Picture a walled garden where teachers walk and argue.
abstract.cn: 想象一座围起来的花园，教师在其中散步争论。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor of offices, each with a stack of papers.
abstract.cn: 想象一条办公室走廊，每间都堆着论文。

abstract.en: Picture two doors labelled campus and company.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇门，分别写着校园与公司。

examples.en: She spent twenty years in academia before joining a lab.
examples.cn: 她在学术界待了二十年才加入一家实验室。

examples.en: Many researchers leave academia because of short contracts.
examples.cn: 许多研究者因短期合同离开学术圈。

examples.en: The gap between academia and industry is narrowing.
examples.cn: 学术界与产业界之间的差距正在缩小。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卡德米亚」——柏拉图讲学的那片园子，后来成了整个世界：学术界。

root: 古希腊 Akademicia（阿卡德摩斯园林）→ 拉丁语 academia（柏拉图学园）；核心义是「学者聚集从事研究的那个世界」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the institutions of learning as one world, to the career and working life inside them.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从把学术机构看作一个整体世界，走到其中的职业与工作生活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a separate world built of lecture halls, libraries, and labs
core.cn: 核心意象：由讲堂、图书馆与实验室构成的独立世界

branches.en: All institutions of higher learning taken as one body.
branches.cn: 所有高等教育机构合为一个整体。

branches.en: The working life and career path of scholars.
branches.cn: 学者的工作生活与职业路径。

branches.en: The institutions and the career share the same name.
branches.cn: 机构与职业共用同一个名称。

branches.en: A career shapes the culture of the institutions.
branches.cn: 职业塑造了机构的文化。

branches.en: The old grove became both a place and a way of life.
branches.cn: 古老的园林既成了场所，也成了生活方式。

intro.en: The word is a Latin place name turned mass noun; its family grows with the adjective, adverb, and person endings -ic, -ally, and -ician.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁地名词转为集合名词；词族以 -ic、-ally、-ician 等后缀生长。

latinIntro.en: Latin academia is the direct ancestor and names Plato's school, so the Latin entries record that noun and its adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 academia 是直接祖先，指柏拉图学园，因此拉丁条目记录该名词与形容词。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「学术的；学院的」
名词，义为「院士」

definition_zh: 学术的；学院的；纯理论的；大学教师；学者
definition_en: relating to study, teaching, or research, existing only in theory, or a person who teaches and researches at a university
core_image: 讲台、论文与图书馆构成的日常
scene: 招聘广告要求申请人有教学经验，并能发表经过同行评议的论文。The post requires a strong academic record.
sceneCN: 这里 academic 是「学术的」（第 1 个义项：与学习、教学、研究有关）；句意为该职位要求出色的学术履历。

pos.zh: 学术的；学院的；纯理论的

collocations.zh: 纯理论的、无实际意义的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「学业上；学术上」
由同一词根构成，义为「学术界」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「院士」

senses.title: Relating to study and research
senses.definition: connected with education, scholarship, or research rather than with practical business
senses.definitionCN: 与教育、学问或研究相关，而非与实务相关
senses.example: Her academic record earned her a scholarship.
senses.exampleCN: 她的学业成绩为她赢得了奖学金。
senses.why: The adjective comes from the name of Plato's school, so it labels whatever belongs to formal learning and its institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词来自柏拉图学园的名称，因此它标记一切属于正规学问及其机构的事物。

senses.title: Theoretical rather than practical
senses.titleCN: 纯理论的；无实际意义的
senses.definition: existing only in argument or theory, with no practical consequence
senses.definitionCN: 只存在于论证或理论中，没有实际后果
senses.example: Whether the rule applies here is purely academic.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则是否适用于此处，纯属理论问题。
senses.why: When a question has no bearing on action, it stays inside the classroom, so academic becomes a mild word for 'uselessly theoretical'.
senses.whyCN: 当一个问题对行动没有影响，它就留在课堂之内，于是 academic 成了「空谈理论」的委婉说法。

senses.title: A university teacher or researcher
senses.definition: a person whose job is to teach and research at a university
senses.definitionCN: 在大学从事教学与研究的人
senses.example: The department hired three young academics.
senses.exampleCN: 该系聘用了三位年轻的学者。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for the people who live inside that world, much as academia names the world itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为名词，指生活在这个世界内部的人，正如 academia 指这个世界本身。

intro.en: Academic comes from the name of Plato's grove, Akademeia, by way of Latin and French.
intro.cn: academic 来自柏拉图园林的名称 Akademeia，经拉丁语与法语传入。

items.en: The grove outside Athens was named after the hero Akademos.
items.cn: 雅典城外的园林以英雄阿卡德摩斯命名。

items.en: Plato's followers were called Akademikoi, 'those of the Academy'.
items.cn: 柏拉图的门徒被称作 Akademikoi，即「学园中人」。

items.en: Latin academicus meant 'of the Academy'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 academicus 意为「学园的」。

items.en: French académique extended the word to learned societies.
items.cn: 法语 académique 把词义扩展到学术团体。

items.en: English academic first described things belonging to a place of learning.
items.cn: 英语 academic 先描述属于学府的事物。

items.en: Modern usage adds the noun for a university teacher and the sense 'merely theoretical'.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了指大学教师的名词，以及「纯理论」义。

note.en: The first group gathers same-family nouns and the adverb; the second gathers words for scholars and for theory.
note.cn: 第一组收同族名词与副词；第二组收表示学者与理论的词。

entries.definition: The scholarly world as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学术界」，整个学术世界。

entries.definition: A member of a learned academy or society.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「院士」，学术机构成员。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in relation to study'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「学业上；学术上」。

entries.definition: An adjective for careful, learned work.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「学术性的、博学的」，指严谨有学问的工作。

entries.definition: An adjective for anything connected with teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「教育的」，与教学有关。

entries.definition: An adjective for ideas rather than practice.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「理论的」，指观念而非实践。

entries.definition: A person who studies a subject deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学者」，深入研究某学科的人。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Academy origin and the campus collocations; the abstract hooks picture a lectern surrounded by journals.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用学园来源与校园搭配；抽象记忆点想象被期刊围住的讲台。

normal.en: Academic comes from Plato's Academy, so it belongs to formal learning.
normal.cn: academic 来自柏拉图的学园，因此属于正规学问。

normal.en: Academic year and academic performance are everyday campus phrases.
normal.cn: academic year 与 academic performance 是日常校园短语。

normal.en: Purely academic means the question has no practical effect.
normal.cn: purely academic 意为这个问题没有实际影响。

normal.en: An academic can be a person: a university teacher or researcher.
normal.cn: an academic 可以指人：大学教师或研究者。

normal.en: The adverb is academically and the world is academia.
normal.cn: 副词是 academically，那个世界是 academia。

abstract.en: Picture a lectern with three journals stacked beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象讲台旁堆着三本期刊。

abstract.en: Picture an argument that never leaves the seminar room.
abstract.cn: 想象一场从未走出研讨室的争论。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor of offices with names on the doors.
abstract.cn: 想象一条办公室走廊，门上写着名字。

examples.en: The library holds every major academic journal in the field.
examples.cn: 该图书馆收藏了这一领域所有主要学术期刊。

examples.en: Without funding, the dispute remains academic.
examples.cn: 没有经费，这场争论仍只是纸上谈兵。

examples.en: Several academics signed the open letter.
examples.cn: 几位学者签署了那封公开信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卡德米克」——学园里的人、学园里的事，都是学术的。

root: 古希腊 Akademeia（柏拉图学园）→ 拉丁 academicus → 英语 academic；核心义是「属于正规学问与学府的」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from everything belonging to formal study, to theory with no practical use, to the people who work in that world.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从属于正规学问的一切，走到没有实用价值的理论，再到在那个世界工作的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lectern, a library, and papers in progress
core.cn: 核心意象：讲台、图书馆与正在写的论文

branches.en: Anything that belongs to formal study and teaching.
branches.cn: 属于正规学习与教学的一切。

branches.en: A question kept inside theory where it changes nothing.
branches.cn: 被留在理论里、不改变现实的问题。

branches.en: The person whose working life is teaching and research.
branches.cn: 以教学与研究为职业生活的人。

branches.en: The adjective for the work and the noun for the worker share one root.
branches.cn: 描述工作的形容词与指人的名词共享同一词根。

branches.en: Theoretical work is academic work seen from outside.
branches.cn: 理论工作是从外部看到的学术工作。

intro.en: The word is built from the Akademeia stem with adjective, adverb, and person endings, and it also yields the world noun academia.
intro.cn: 这个词由 Akademeia 词干加形容词、副词与人物后缀构成，并衍生出指世界的名词 academia。

latinIntro.en: Latin academicus is the direct ancestor, formed from academia, so the Latin entries record both.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 academicus 是直接祖先，由 academia 构成，因此拉丁条目两者都收。

名词，义为「院士」

definition_zh: 加速；使加快；促进；提前发生
definition_en: to move or make something move faster, or to make an event happen sooner
core_image: 踏板被踩下，车速表指针向右甩
scene: 司机看到前方路况变好，轻踩油门，车子很快并入快车道。The car accelerated smoothly onto the motorway.
sceneCN: 这里 accelerate 是「加速」（第 1 个义项：使移动速度变快）；句意为车子平稳加速驶入高速公路。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「加速；加速度」
由本词加工具后缀构成，义为「加速器；油门」
由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「加速的；提前的」

senses.title: To move faster
senses.definition: to increase the speed of a vehicle, a process, or a movement
senses.definitionCN: 提高车辆、过程或运动的速度
senses.example: The train accelerated as it left the station.
senses.exampleCN: 火车离站时逐渐加速。
senses.why: Latin accelerare joined ad- 'to' with celer 'swift', so the verb means 'to bring speed to' something.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accelerare 由 ad-（向）与 celer（迅速）组成，因此这个动词意为「把速度加给某物」。

senses.title: To make an event happen sooner
senses.definition: to cause something to occur earlier or more quickly
senses.definitionCN: 使某事更早或更快地发生
senses.example: The new rules accelerated the approval of small projects.
senses.exampleCN: 新规加快了小型项目的审批。
senses.why: The speed image transfers from motion to time: if a process moves faster along its course, its end arrives sooner.
senses.whyCN: 速度意象从运动转到时间：过程在途中走得更快，终点就会更早到达。

senses.title: To gain speed in physics
senses.definition: of a body, to change velocity, especially to increase it
senses.definitionCN: 指物体速度发生变化，尤指增大
senses.example: The particle accelerates as it approaches the field.
senses.exampleCN: 粒子接近场时加速。
senses.why: Physics gives the word a precise measure, acceleration, distinguishing steady motion from changing velocity.
senses.whyCN: 物理学为这个词给出精确的量度 acceleration，把匀速运动与速度变化区分开来。

intro.en: Accelerate is Latin accelerare, from ad- 'to' and celer 'swift, quick'.
intro.cn: accelerate 即拉丁语 accelerare，由 ad-（向）与 celer（迅速）构成。

items.en: celer meant 'swift' and survives in celerity, 'speed'.
items.cn: celer 意为「迅速」，仍见于 celerity（快速）。

items.en: accelerare meant 'to hasten, bring speed to'.
items.cn: accelerare 意为「催促、使加快」。

items.en: acceleratio named the act of hastening.
items.cn: acceleratio 指催促的动作。

items.en: English accelerate first meant to hasten an action or event.
items.cn: 英语 accelerate 最初指催促行动或事件。

items.en: With mechanics, acceleration became a measured change of velocity.
items.cn: 随力学发展，acceleration 成为可测量的速度变化。

items.en: Modern usage extends the verb to economic growth and project schedules.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个动词扩展到经济增长与项目进度。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, the device word, and the participle; the second gathers verbs for increasing speed.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、装置词与分词；第二组收表示提高速度的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for increasing speed, or the rate of change of velocity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加速」或「加速度」。

entries.definition: A device that increases speed, such as a pedal or a machine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加速器、油门」，提高速度的装置。

entries.definition: An adjective for something made faster or moved earlier.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「加速的、提前的」。

entries.definition: A formal noun meaning speed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，正式用法，义为「迅速」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to make something happen sooner.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「促使、加快」。

entries.definition: A phrasal verb meaning to go or make go faster.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「加快」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to make a process run more quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加快办理」，使流程更快。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to become or make quicker.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加快」，变得更迅速。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin 'swift' root and the growth collocations; the abstract hooks picture the needle swinging right.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁语「迅速」词根与增长搭配；抽象记忆点想象指针向右甩。

normal.en: Accelerate holds Latin celer, 'swift', the root of celerity.
normal.cn: accelerate 含有拉丁语 celer（迅速），即 celerity 的词根。

normal.en: Accelerate growth and accelerate the process are the standard patterns.
normal.cn: accelerate growth 与 accelerate the process 是标准搭配。

normal.en: The noun is acceleration, the device an accelerator.
normal.cn: 名词是 acceleration，装置是 accelerator。

normal.en: In physics, acceleration is change of velocity, not just more speed.
normal.cn: 物理学中 acceleration 是速度的变化，不只是变快。

normal.en: The opposite is decelerate, built with de- 'down'.
normal.cn: 反义词是 decelerate，由 de-（向下）构成。

abstract.en: Picture a foot pressing a pedal and the needle leaping right.
abstract.cn: 想象脚踩踏板，指针向右跳。

abstract.en: Picture a queue moving twice as fast after a second window opens.
abstract.cn: 想象第二个窗口开启后队伍快了一倍。

abstract.en: Picture a particle pulled harder as it nears a magnet.
abstract.cn: 想象粒子接近磁体时被拉得更紧。

examples.en: Digital tools have accelerated the pace of research.
examples.cn: 数字工具加快了研究节奏。

examples.en: The bus accelerated away from the stop.
examples.cn: 公交车加速驶离站台。

examples.en: Warmer air accelerates the melting of the glacier.
examples.cn: 较暖的空气加速冰川融化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞勒瑞特」——脚踩油门，指针向右甩，就是加速。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ celer（迅速）→ accelerare（使加快）；核心义是「把速度加上去」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from physical speed, to time saved in a process, to the measured change of velocity in physics.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从物理速度，走到流程中节省的时间，再到物理学中有量度的速度变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle swinging right as the pedal goes down
core.cn: 核心意象：踏板踩下、指针向右甩

branches.en: A vehicle or process moving faster.
branches.cn: 车辆或过程移动得更快。

branches.en: A process reaching its end sooner.
branches.cn: 过程更早到达终点。

branches.en: A physical body whose velocity changes measurably.
branches.cn: 速度发生可测量变化的物体。

branches.en: Speed in motion becomes speed in time.
branches.cn: 运动中的速度转为时间上的提前。

branches.en: Both senses treat speed as something that can be measured and increased.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把速度视为可测量、可提高之物。

intro.en: The verb joins the Latin prefix ad- with the swift root celer-, and its family adds the action, device, and participle endings.
intro.cn: 这个动词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与「迅速」词根 celer- 结合，词族再加动作、装置与分词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin accelerare is the direct ancestor, together with the noun acceleratio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accelerare 是直接祖先，名词 acceleratio 同时。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「加速；加速度」
名词，义为「加速器；油门」

definition_zh: 油门；加速器；促进因素
definition_en: a pedal that increases a vehicle's speed, a machine that speeds up particles, or anything that makes a process happen faster
core_image: 一个被踩下去就把速度加上去的装置
scene: 上坡时司机把脚下的踏板踩深一点，车子才不至于慢下来。She pressed the accelerator to climb the hill.
sceneCN: 这里 accelerator 是「油门踏板」（第 1 个义项：车辆中提高速度的踏板）；句意为她踩下油门爬坡。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词词根，义为「加速」
同源名词，义为「加速；加速度」

senses.title: A vehicle's speed pedal
senses.definition: the pedal in a car or other vehicle that increases engine power and speed
senses.definitionCN: 汽车等交通工具中提高动力与速度的踏板
senses.example: He kept his foot off the accelerator while reversing.
senses.exampleCN: 倒车时他一直把脚离开油门。
senses.why: The -or ending marks a device, so accelerator names the part whose whole job is to add speed.
senses.whyCN: -or 后缀标记装置，因此 accelerator 指专门用来加速的部件。

senses.title: A machine for speeding up particles
senses.definition: a large apparatus that drives particles to very high speeds for research or treatment
senses.definitionCN: 把粒子加速到极高速度、用于研究或治疗的大型装置
senses.example: The new accelerator can reach energies once thought impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 新加速器能达到曾被认为不可能的能量。
senses.why: Physicists took the everyday device word and gave it to the giant ring that accelerates particles to enormous velocity.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家把这个日常装置词给了把粒子加速到极高速度的巨型环状设备。

senses.title: Something that speeds up a process
senses.definition: anything that causes a process or change to happen faster
senses.definitionCN: 使某过程或变化发生得更快的事物
senses.example: Cheap credit acted as an accelerator for the housing boom.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价信贷成了房地产热潮的加速剂。
senses.why: Because the word already means a device for adding speed, it easily names abstract forces that play the same part.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词本义就是「加快速度的装置」，它很容易用来指起同样作用的抽象力量。

intro.en: Accelerator is the Latin agent noun of accelerare, marked by the -or ending for a thing that acts.
intro.cn: accelerator 是 accelerare 的拉丁语施动名词，由 -or 后缀标记施动之物。

items.en: celer meant 'swift', the root shared with celerity.
items.cn: celer 意为「迅速」，与 celerity 共享词根。

items.en: accelerare meant 'to hasten or add speed'.
items.cn: accelerare 意为「催促、加速」。

items.en: The agent ending -or named a person or thing that performs an action.
items.cn: 施动后缀 -or 指执行动作的人或物。

items.en: Early English accelerator named a person who hastened matters.
items.cn: 早期英语 accelerator 指催促事务的人。

items.en: With engines and machinery, the word shifted to the speed control.
items.cn: 随发动机与机械发展，词义转向速度控制装置。

items.en: Physics applied it to machines that drive particles near light speed.
items.cn: 物理学家把它用于把粒子加速到接近光速的机器。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb and the noun from the same family; the second gathers words for speed controls and for things that hasten.
note.cn: 第一组收同族动词与名词；第二组收表示速度控制与促动之物。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to increase speed or bring forward.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加速」或「提前」。

entries.definition: The noun for the process or the physical quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加速」或「加速度」。

entries.definition: An adjective for a process that has been speeded up.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「加速的、提前的」。

entries.definition: A device or pedal controlling engine power.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「节流阀、油门」，控制发动机功率的装置。

entries.definition: A foot-operated lever in a vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「踏板」，用车脚踏动的杆。

entries.definition: Something that triggers or speeds up change.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「催化剂、促发因素」。

entries.definition: Something that increases power or support.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「助推器、增强物」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -or device ending and the driving phrases; the abstract hooks picture a pedal that hands speed to the machine.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 -or 装置后缀与驾驶搭配；抽象记忆点想象把速度交给机器的踏板。

normal.en: Accelerator is accelerate plus -or, the ending for a device.
normal.cn: accelerator 是 accelerate 加 -or，表示装置的词尾。

normal.en: Press the accelerator and release the accelerator are driving phrases.
normal.cn: press the accelerator 与 release the accelerator 是驾驶用语。

normal.en: A particle accelerator is a giant ring, not a car part.
normal.cn: particle accelerator 是巨型环状设备，不是汽车零件。

normal.en: The British also call the pedal the gas pedal.
normal.cn: 英式英语中这个踏板也叫 gas pedal。

normal.en: The word works for abstract forces too: an accelerator of growth.
normal.cn: 这个词也用于抽象力量：an accelerator of growth。

abstract.en: Picture a foot pressing a pedal and the engine answering with a roar.
abstract.cn: 想象脚踩踏板，发动机以轰鸣回应。

abstract.en: Picture a huge ring under the ground pushing particles in circles.
abstract.cn: 想象地下巨型环把粒子一圈圈推快。

abstract.en: Picture cheap credit pouring fuel on a housing boom.
abstract.cn: 想象廉价信贷给房地产热潮添柴。

examples.en: She pressed the accelerator too hard on the wet road.
examples.cn: 在湿滑路面上她把油门踩得太狠。

examples.en: The laboratory built a new particle accelerator last year.
examples.cn: 实验室去年建成了一台新的粒子加速器。

examples.en: Better transport became an accelerator of regional trade.
examples.cn: 更便利的交通成了区域贸易的加速剂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞勒瑞特」——专门把速度加上去的那个装置，就是油门或加速器。

root: 拉丁语 accelerare（加速）+ 施动后缀 -or；核心义是「专职增加速度的装置」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the vehicle pedal, to the research machine, to any force that hastens a process.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从车辆踏板，走到研究装置，再到任何加快过程的抽象力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a device whose only job is to add speed
core.cn: 核心意象：唯一职责就是增加速度的装置

branches.en: The pedal that answers the driver's foot.
branches.cn: 回应司机脚下的踏板。

branches.en: The ring that drives particles to extreme speed.
branches.cn: 把粒子推向极速的环状设备。

branches.en: An abstract force that plays the same part in a process.
branches.cn: 在过程中起同样作用的抽象力量。

branches.en: Both are machines built only for speed.
branches.cn: 两者都是只为速度而造的机器。

branches.en: Research machines and market forces both act as accelerators.
branches.cn: 研究装置与市场力量都充当加速剂。

intro.en: The word is accelerate with the agent ending -or, and the family also contains the verb and the action noun.
intro.cn: 这个词是 accelerate 加施动后缀 -or，词族还含动词与动作名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin accelerare plus the agent suffix -or produced the form, so the Latin entries record the verb and its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accelerare 加持动后缀 -or 构成此形，因此拉丁条目记录动词与其名词。

definition_zh: 强调；使突出；重读
definition_en: to emphasize something or make a feature more noticeable, or to place stress on a syllable
core_image: 给一幅画最关键的那一笔再描一遍深色
scene: 摄影师让模特侧身站立，深色背景把她的轮廓衬得更清楚。The dark background accentuates her outline.
sceneCN: 这里 accentuate 是「使突出」（第 1 个义项：让某特征更明显）；句意为深色背景突出了她的轮廓。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「强调；重读」
由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「被突出的」

senses.title: To emphasize a point
senses.definition: to give more weight or attention to an idea or fact
senses.definitionCN: 对一个观点或事实给予更多分量或注意
senses.example: The report accentuates the risks rather than the gains.
senses.exampleCN: 报告着重讲风险，而非收益。
senses.why: Latin accentus meant 'a song added to', a musical stress; to accentuate is to add that extra weight to a word or a point.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accentus 意为「附加的歌声」，即语气上的加重；accentuate 就是把这份额外分量加到词或观点上。

senses.title: To make a feature stand out
senses.definition: to make a visible quality or shape more noticeable
senses.definitionCN: 使可见的性质或形状更显眼
senses.example: The bright scarf accentuates the grey coat.
senses.exampleCN: 亮色围巾把灰色大衣衬得更醒目。
senses.why: The same added weight can be visual: contrast and line make one element draw the eye first.
senses.whyCN: 同样的额外分量也可以是视觉上的：对比与线条让某一元素先吸引目光。

senses.title: To stress a syllable
senses.definition: to pronounce a syllable with greater force
senses.definitionCN: 用更大的力度发出某个音节
senses.example: In this word, you accentuate the second syllable.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个词里，你要重读第二个音节。
senses.why: The oldest sense stays closest to accentus: speech gives one syllable a stronger beat, as music gives one note a stronger beat.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项最贴近 accentus：说话给某个音节更强的节拍，正如音乐给某个音更强的节拍。

intro.en: Accentuate comes from Latin accentus, 'a song added', a translation of the Greek word for musical accent.
intro.cn: accentuate 来自拉丁语 accentus（附加的歌声），是希腊语「乐调」一词的译借。

items.en: canere meant 'to sing', the source of cantare and chant.
items.cn: canere 意为「唱」，是 cantare 与 chant 的来源。

items.en: accentus literally meant 'a singing added to', a vocal or musical stress.
items.cn: accentus 字面意为「附加的唱」，指语音或音乐上的重音。

items.en: Later Latin accentuare meant 'to give accent to'.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 accentuare 意为「给……加重音」。

items.en: French accentu-er carried the verb into modern use.
items.cn: 法语 accentuer 把这个动词带入现代用法。

items.en: English accentuate first meant to pronounce with stress.
items.cn: 英语 accentuate 最初指加重音读。

items.en: Modern usage extends it to emphasizing ideas and visible features.
items.cn: 现代用法把它扩展到强调观点与可见特征。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun and participle plus the base noun accent; the second gathers verbs of emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、分词与基础名词 accent；第二组收表示强调的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of emphasizing or stressing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「强调；重读」。

entries.definition: The stress or the pronunciation style of a language.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「重音」或「口音」。

entries.definition: An adjective for a feature made more noticeable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被突出的」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to give special importance to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「强调」，给予特别重要性。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to draw attention to a part.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「突出、标出」，把注意力引向某部分。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to stress something strongly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「强调」，语气较强。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to pronounce or emphasize with force.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「重读、强调」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'song added' origin and the visual phrases; the abstract hooks picture one line redrawn darker.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「附加歌声」来源与视觉搭配；抽象记忆点想象把一根线描得更深。

normal.en: Accentuate is accent plus a verb ending: to add extra weight.
normal.cn: accentuate 是 accent 加动词后缀：加上额外分量。

normal.en: Accentuate the difference and accentuate the positive are common phrases.
normal.cn: accentuate the difference 与 accentuate the positive 是常见短语。

normal.en: In speech, to accentuate a syllable is to beat it harder.
normal.cn: 口语中重读某个音节就是给它更重的节拍。

normal.en: The noun is accentuation, formed with -tion.
normal.cn: 名词是 accentuation，由 -tion 构成。

normal.en: Latin accentus meant a song added to the voice.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 accentus 意为加在声音上的歌。

abstract.en: Picture one line in a drawing traced again in darker ink.
abstract.cn: 想象画中的一根线被更深的墨再描一遍。

abstract.en: Picture a bright scarf against a grey coat.
abstract.cn: 想象灰大衣上的亮色围巾。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker hitting one syllable harder than the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象说话者把某个音节打得比其余更重。

examples.en: The new evidence accentuates the need for reform.
examples.cn: 新证据凸显了改革的必要。

examples.en: Vertical stripes accentuate the height of the room.
examples.cn: 竖条纹使房间显得更高。

examples.en: Try to accentuate the first syllable in this word.
examples.cn: 试着重读这个词的第一个音节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克森图埃特」——像给一句歌加重拍，或给一条线加深色，就是强调。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ canere（唱）→ accentus（附加的歌声）→ accentuare；核心义是「加上额外分量」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from spoken stress, to emphasis on an idea, to making a visible feature stand out.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从口语重音，走到对观点的着重，再到让可见特征更醒目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one line in the picture traced again in darker ink
core.cn: 核心意象：画中被更深墨再描一遍的那根线

branches.en: An idea given extra weight in an argument.
branches.cn: 在论证中被给予额外分量的观点。

branches.en: A visible feature made stronger by contrast.
branches.cn: 靠对比而更醒目的可见特征。

branches.en: A syllable given a stronger beat in speech.
branches.cn: 在口语中被给予更强节拍的音节。

branches.en: Emphasis works the same way for the ear and the eye.
branches.cn: 强调对耳朵与眼睛的作用方式相同。

branches.en: Spoken stress is the model for emphasizing ideas.
branches.cn: 口语重音是强调观点所依据的模型。

intro.en: The word joins the singing root can- with the prefix ad-, and its family adds the action and participle endings.
intro.cn: 这个词把「唱」词根 can- 与前缀 ad- 结合，词族另加动作与分词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin accentus and accentuare are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the noun and the verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accentus 与 accentuare 是直接祖先，因此拉丁条目记录名词与动词。
