definition_zh: 可接受的；尚可的；合乎要求的
definition_en: good enough to be agreed to or tolerated, satisfactory though not excellent, or allowed by a standard
core_image: 一份交上去的文件，被对方点头收下
scene: 提案改到第三版，预算仍偏高，但委员会认为已经可以勉强通过。The revised plan is now acceptable to the board.
sceneCN: 这里 acceptable 是「可接受的」（第 1 个义项：好到能被同意或容忍）；句意为修订后的方案现在董事会可以接受。

pos.zh: 可接受的；尚可的；合乎要求的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「可接受地」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「可接受性」
同源名词，义为「接受；接纳」

senses.title: Good enough to be agreed to
senses.titleCN: 可接受的；能让人同意的
senses.definition: of a plan, offer, or condition, good enough that someone will agree to it
senses.definitionCN: 指方案、提议或条件好到有人愿意同意
senses.example: Both sides finally found an acceptable compromise.
senses.exampleCN: 双方终于找到一个可以接受的折中方案。
senses.why: The suffix -able marks what can be done: acceptable is what can be accepted, so it sits at the threshold of agreement.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 标记「能够被……的」：acceptable 即能够被接受之物，站在同意的门槛上。

senses.title: Satisfactory but not good
senses.definition: meeting a minimum standard without being impressive
senses.definitionCN: 达到最低标准但并不出色
senses.example: The food was acceptable, though nothing special.
senses.exampleCN: 饭菜还过得去，但没什么特别。
senses.why: Something that merely passes the bar is accepted without praise, so the word often carries a faint shrug.
senses.whyCN: 仅仅越过门槛的东西会被接受但不会受称赞，因此这个词常带一点「勉强」的意味。

senses.title: Allowed by a standard
senses.definition: conforming to rules or to what a group considers proper
senses.definitionCN: 符合规则或群体认为得体的标准
senses.example: Such language is not acceptable in a formal report.
senses.exampleCN: 这种措辞在正式报告中是不合要求的。
senses.why: Acceptance by a community depends on shared norms, so acceptable comes to mean 'within the rules' rather than merely 'liked'.
senses.whyCN: 被群体接受取决于共同规范，因此 acceptable 指「在规则之内」，而不只是「被喜欢」。

intro.en: Acceptable adds the Latin suffix -abilis, 'that can be', to the verb accept.
intro.cn: acceptable 在动词 accept 上加拉丁语后缀 -abilis（能够被……的）。

items.en: capere meant 'to take', the root behind accept, receive, and capture.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿、取」，是 accept、receive 与 capture 的词根。

items.en: accipere meant 'to take to oneself, receive'.
items.cn: accipere 意为「接受、收下」。

items.en: acceptare was the frequentative form, 'to keep receiving, to approve'.
items.cn: acceptare 是反复形式，意为「一再接收、认可」。

items.en: The suffix -abilis marked what is possible or fit to be done.
items.cn: 后缀 -abilis 标记可能或适合被做之事。

items.en: Old French formed acceptable with the same 'can be received' sense.
items.cn: 古法语以同一「能被接收」义构成 acceptable。

items.en: English acceptable first described offerings and terms fit to be received.
items.cn: 英语 acceptable 先描述适合被接受的献礼与条件。

note.en: The first group gathers the negative form and related adjectives and nouns; the second gathers words for what is good enough.
note.cn: 第一组收否定形式与相关形容词、名词；第二组收表示「够得上标准」的词。

entries.definition: The negative adjective for what cannot be allowed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词否定形式，义为「不可接受的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for something already approved by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「已被普遍接受的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or state of being received.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接受、接纳」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'to a tolerable degree'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「可接受地」。

entries.definition: An adjective for something that meets a requirement.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人满意的」，达到要求。

entries.definition: An adjective for something that can be endured.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可忍受的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for something rules allow.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可允许的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for something just good enough.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「勉强合格的、过得去的」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -able 'can be' rule and the board phrases; the abstract hooks picture a stamped sheet handed back.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 -able「能够被」规则与委员会搭配；抽象记忆点想象盖了章的文件被递回。

normal.en: Acceptable is accept plus -able: able to be accepted.
normal.cn: acceptable 是 accept 加 -able：能够被接受。

normal.en: Acceptable to the board is the usual preposition pattern.
normal.cn: acceptable to the board 是常见的介词结构。

normal.en: Socially acceptable describes behaviour within shared norms.
normal.cn: socially acceptable 描述符合共同规范的行为。

normal.en: The negative form is unacceptable, very common in rules.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 unacceptable，在规则中很常见。

normal.en: The noun is acceptance, not acceptation, in everyday use.
normal.cn: 日常用法中名词是 acceptance，而非 acceptation。

abstract.en: Picture a committee nodding once and pushing the file back.
abstract.cn: 想象委员会点一下头，把文件推回来。

abstract.en: Picture a dish that is eaten without complaint and without praise.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘菜被吃完，既无抱怨也无称赞。

abstract.en: Picture a sign listing what is allowed inside a building.
abstract.cn: 想象一块列明楼内许可事项的告示牌。

examples.en: The offer was acceptable to both unions.
examples.cn: 这个提议两个工会都能接受。

examples.en: Conditions in the hostel were acceptable but basic.
examples.cn: 旅馆条件尚可，但很简陋。

examples.en: Late submission is acceptable only with written permission.
examples.cn: 只有获得书面许可，迟交才被允许。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞普特波」——递上去被人点头收下，就是可接受的。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ capere（拿）→ accipere（收下）→ acceptare + -abilis（能被……的）；核心义是「够得上被接受的门槛」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from what can be agreed to, to what merely passes, to what a community's rules allow.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从能被同意之物，走到仅仅及格之物，再到社群规则允许之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a file nodded through and handed back
core.cn: 核心意象：被点头通过并递回的文件

branches.en: A proposal good enough for agreement.
branches.cn: 好到足以达成同意的提案。

branches.en: A result that clears the bar without praise.
branches.cn: 越过门槛但不受称赞的结果。

branches.en: Behaviour that stays inside shared norms.
branches.cn: 停留在共同规范之内的行为。

branches.en: Agreement and permission both depend on an outside judge.
branches.cn: 同意与许可都取决于外部评判者。

branches.en: The plain sense and the lukewarm sense share one threshold.
branches.cn: 普通义与勉强的语气共享同一个门槛。

intro.en: The word joins the take root cap- with the prefix ad- and the possibility suffix -able, and its family adds noun and adverb forms.
intro.cn: 这个词把「取」词根 cap- 与前缀 ad-、可能性后缀 -able 结合，词族另加名词与副词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin acceptare and the suffix -abilis combined to form the word, so the Latin entries record the verb and the suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 acceptare 与后缀 -abilis 组合成词，因此拉丁条目记录动词与后缀。

definition_en: a way in, the right or chance to use something, or to reach and open data
core_image: 一扇门或一条小路，通向本来进不去的地方
scene: 图书馆把旧期刊移到地下室，读者要先在系统里预约，才能进去取阅。Students need a pass for access to the archive.
sceneCN: 这里 access 是「进入权、使用权」（第 1 个义项：获准进入或使用某处）；句意为学生需要通行证才能进入档案室。

pos.zh: 通道；进入权；使用权；访问

collocations.zh: 进入……的机会；使用……的途径

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「可进入的；易理解的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「可及性；无障碍程度」
同源名词，义为「加入；就职；入藏」

senses.title: A way in or through
senses.definition: a means of entering a place or reaching something
senses.definitionCN: 进入某地或到达某物的途径
senses.example: The only access to the village is a narrow track.
senses.exampleCN: 通往村子的唯一通道是一条窄道。
senses.why: Latin accessus meant 'a coming near'; the physical approach to a place is the first thing the word names.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessus 意为「走近」；到达某地的物理路径是这个词最先命名的东西。

senses.title: The right or chance to use something
senses.definition: permission or opportunity to use a service, a person, or a resource
senses.definitionCN: 使用某项服务、某个人或某种资源的许可或机会
senses.example: Students have free access to the online journals.
senses.exampleCN: 学生可以免费使用这些在线期刊。
senses.why: Once a way in exists, the word shifts from the path to the permission that lets someone walk it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了入口，这个词就从路径转向让人走进去的许可。

senses.title: To reach and open stored data
senses.definition: to find, open, or retrieve information held in a system
senses.definitionCN: 在系统中查找、打开或取出信息
senses.example: The program accesses the file only after you log in.
senses.exampleCN: 只有登录后程序才会访问该文件。
senses.why: Computing treats stored files as rooms behind a door, so the verb keeps the old entering image for data.
senses.whyCN: 计算机把存储的文件视为门后的房间，因此动词把古老的「进入」意象用在数据上。

senses.title: A sudden fit or outburst
senses.definition: an attack of illness or a burst of strong feeling, in older use
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法中疾病的发作或强烈情绪的突发
senses.example: In a sudden access of rage he threw the papers down.
senses.exampleCN: 他一阵暴怒，把文件扔在地上。
senses.why: This rare sense comes from a different Latin noun for a fever's onset; it survives mainly in literary writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个罕见义来自另一个表示「发热发作」的拉丁名词；主要残存于文学写作。

intro.en: Access comes from Latin accessus, 'a coming near', from accedere, 'to go toward'.
intro.cn: access 来自拉丁语 accessus（走近），源自动词 accedere（向……走）。

items.en: cedere meant 'to go, yield', also behind proceed and recess.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走、让」，也构成 proceed 与 recess。

items.en: accedere meant 'to go toward, approach'.
items.cn: accedere 意为「走向、接近」。

items.en: accessus was the noun 'a coming near, an approach'.
items.cn: accessus 是名词，意为「走近、接近」。

items.en: French accès carried both the approach and the right to enter.
items.cn: 法语 accès 同时带「接近」与「进入权」义。

items.en: English access first named the act of approaching or a way in.
items.cn: 英语 access 先指接近的动作或进入的途径。

items.en: Modern usage adds the right to use services and the computing verb.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了使用服务的权利与计算机动词。

note.en: The first group gathers the adjective, its noun, and the related noun accession; the second gathers words for entry and permission.
note.cn: 第一组收形容词、其名词与相关名词 accession；第二组收表示进入与许可的词。

entries.definition: An adjective for something easy to reach or understand.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可到达的；易理解的」。

entries.definition: The noun for how easily something can be reached or used.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可及性」，某事可被到达或使用的容易程度。

entries.definition: The act of coming to office or of adding to a collection.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就职；入藏」。

entries.definition: A road built to reach a place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「进入道路」。

entries.definition: The act or right of entering a place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入」或「进入权」。

entries.definition: Permission to enter a place or join a group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「准许进入、接纳」。

entries.definition: The act of coming near, or a way of dealing with something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接近」或「方法」。

entries.definition: The state of being ready to be used.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可获得性」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin 'go toward' root and the fixed to-pattern; the abstract hooks picture a narrow track leading to a walled village.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁语「走向」词根与固定 to 结构；抽象记忆点想象通往围村的一条窄道。

normal.en: Access is Latin 'a coming near', from cedere, to go.
normal.cn: access 是拉丁语「走近」，来自 cedere（走）。

normal.en: Access to is the fixed pattern: access to the archive.
normal.cn: access to 是固定结构：access to the archive。

normal.en: Gain access and deny access are the two administrative phrases.
normal.cn: gain access 与 deny access 是两个行政用语。

normal.en: The adjective accessible ends in -ible, not -able.
normal.cn: 形容词 accessible 以 -ible 结尾，不是 -able。

normal.en: Access as a verb is mainly about files and systems.
normal.cn: access 作动词主要涉及文件与系统。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow track through fields to a walled village.
abstract.cn: 想象穿过田野通往围村的一条窄道。

abstract.en: Picture a card that opens one locked door and no other.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只开一扇锁门的卡。

abstract.en: Picture a login box that lets the program into a folder.
abstract.cn: 想象登录框让程序进入一个文件夹。

examples.en: Rural areas still lack access to clean water.
examples.cn: 农村地区仍然缺乏获得清洁水源的途径。

examples.en: Only staff can access the medical records.
examples.cn: 只有员工才能访问医疗记录。

examples.en: A new access road will serve the industrial park.
examples.cn: 一条新的进入道路将服务这个工业园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞斯」——一条通往本来进不去之处的路，就是通道与进入权。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ cedere（走）→ accedere（走近）→ accessus；核心义是「走近并进入的途径与许可」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the physical way in, to the permission to use, to the computing act of opening data, and an older sense of a sudden fit.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从物理通道，走到使用许可，再到计算机中打开数据的动作，以及旧有的「发作」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path or key that lets someone reach what was closed
core.cn: 核心意象：让人抵达原本封闭之处的路或钥匙

branches.en: The physical route into a place.
branches.cn: 进入某地的物理路径。

branches.en: The right or chance to use a resource.
branches.cn: 使用某种资源的权利或机会。

branches.en: The computing act of opening stored information.
branches.cn: 打开存储信息的计算机动作。

branches.en: An older sense of a sudden attack of feeling or illness.
branches.cn: 旧义：情绪或疾病的突然发作。

branches.en: A way in and the right to use it are two halves of one idea.
branches.cn: 入口与使用许可构成同一观念的两半。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin prefix ad- with the going root ced-, and its family adds adjective and noun endings.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与「走」词根 ced- 结合，词族另加形容词与名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin accedere and accessus are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the verb and the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accedere 与 accessus 是直接祖先，因此拉丁条目记录动词与名词。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「可进入的；易理解的」
名词，义为「可及性；无障碍程度」

definition_zh: 可到达的；易得到的；易理解的；无障碍的
definition_en: easy to reach, easy to obtain or use, easy to understand, or designed for people with disabilities
core_image: 一条坡道让轮椅也能顺利进门
scene: 博物馆把正门旁加了缓坡，轮椅和婴儿车都能直接推进展厅。The new entrance makes the gallery accessible to everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 accessible 是「可进入的、无障碍的」（第 1 个义项：容易到达）；句意为新入口让所有人都能进入展厅。

pos.zh: 可到达的；易得到的；易理解的；无障碍的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「可及性；无障碍程度」

同源名词，义为「通道；使用权」

senses.title: Easy to reach
senses.definition: of a place, able to be reached without difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 指某地不难到达
senses.example: The beach is accessible only by boat.
senses.exampleCN: 这片海滩只能乘船到达。
senses.why: The adjective adds -ible, 'can be', to access, so it describes a place where the way in actually works.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在 access 上加 -ible（能够被），因此描述入口真正行得通的地方。

senses.title: Easy to obtain or use
senses.definition: of a service, resource, or price, within most people's reach
senses.definitionCN: 指服务、资源或价格在多数人可及范围内
senses.example: Affordable housing should be accessible to young families.
senses.exampleCN: 可负担住房应当让年轻家庭够得着。
senses.why: Physical reach extends to cost and permission: if nothing blocks the way, the thing is accessible even without a door.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的可及扩展到费用与许可：若没有阻碍，即使没有门，该物也是可获取的。

senses.title: Easy to understand
senses.definition: of writing or speech, clear enough for non-specialists
senses.definitionCN: 指文字或言语清楚到非专业者也能懂
senses.example: She writes in accessible language without losing accuracy.
senses.exampleCN: 她用通俗的语言写作，又不失准确。
senses.why: Understanding is pictured as entering a text; when the door is wide, the reader walks in without a key.
senses.whyCN: 理解被想象为走进文本；门开得宽，读者不用钥匙就能进去。

senses.title: Designed for disabled users
senses.definition: built or fitted so that people with disabilities can use it
senses.definitionCN: 为残障人士使用而建造或改装
senses.example: The station has lifts and an accessible toilet.
senses.exampleCN: 车站设有电梯和无障碍卫生间。
senses.why: Modern design gives the old word a technical sense: a building is accessible when no physical barrier shuts a group out.
senses.whyCN: 现代设计给这个词一个技术义：当没有物理障碍把某群体挡在外面，建筑就是无障碍的。

intro.en: Accessible is access with the Latin possibility suffix -ibilis, meaning 'that can be entered'.
intro.cn: accessible 是 access 加拉丁语可能性后缀 -ibilis，意为「能够被进入的」。

items.en: cedere meant 'to go', the root of accedere and accessus.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走」，是 accedere 与 accessus 的词根。

items.en: accessus meant 'a coming near, an approach'.
items.cn: accessus 意为「走近、接近」。

items.en: The suffix -ibilis marked what is possible or fit to be done.
items.cn: 后缀 -ibilis 标记可能或适合被做之事。

items.en: French formed accessible with the sense 'that can be approached'.
items.cn: 法语构成 accessible，义为「可以被接近的」。

items.en: English accessible first described places that could be entered.
items.cn: 英语 accessible 先描述可以进入的场所。

items.en: Modern usage adds easy reading and barrier-free design.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了易读与无障碍设计两层意思。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adverb, and base noun; the second gathers adjectives for what is within reach.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、副词与基础名词；第二组收表示可及范围的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for how easily something can be reached or used.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可及性」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in an easy-to-reach or easy-to-read way'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「易懂地、可及地」。

entries.definition: The noun for a way in or a right to use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通道；使用权」。

entries.definition: The negative adjective for what cannot be reached.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词否定形式，义为「无法到达的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for a place one can get to.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可到达的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for something ready to be used or obtained.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可获得的、可用的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for something clear enough to grasp.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可理解的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for something not closed to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「开放的」，对公众不封闭。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -ible 'can be' rule and the wheelchair phrases; the abstract hooks picture a ramp beside a steep step.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 -ible「能够被」规则与无障碍搭配；抽象记忆点想象陡台阶旁的缓坡。

normal.en: Accessible is access plus -ible: able to be entered.
normal.cn: accessible 是 access 加 -ible：能够被进入。

normal.en: Accessible to is the fixed preposition: accessible to all.
normal.cn: accessible to 是固定介词结构：accessible to all。

normal.en: Wheelchair accessible is a standard design label.
normal.cn: wheelchair accessible 是标准设计标签。

normal.en: The noun is accessibility, the adverb accessibly.
normal.cn: 名词是 accessibility，副词是 accessibly。

normal.en: The negative is inaccessible, with in- prefixed.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 inaccessible，加前缀 in-。

abstract.en: Picture a gentle ramp beside a steep stone step.
abstract.cn: 想象陡石阶旁的一条缓坡。

abstract.en: Picture a journal with no paywall in front of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本前面没有付费墙的期刊。

abstract.en: Picture a guidebook that explains jargon in plain words.
abstract.cn: 想象一本用大白话解释术语的指南。

examples.en: The temple is accessible by a footpath from the village.
examples.cn: 从村子沿小路可以到达这座庙。

examples.en: The library makes rare books accessible online.
examples.cn: 图书馆让珍本可以在线获取。

examples.en: Her lecture was accessible to students without a science background.
examples.cn: 她的讲座让没有理科背景的学生也听得懂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞斯波」——门口加了缓坡，谁都能进去，就是可到达的。

root: 拉丁语 accedere（走近）+ -ibilis（能够被）；核心义是「进得去、够得着、读得懂」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a place one can reach, to a resource one can use, to a text one can understand, to a building open to disabled users.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从能到达的场所，走到能使用的资源，再到能读懂的文本，最后是对残障者开放的建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ramp that removes the barrier at the door
core.cn: 核心意象：消除门口障碍的缓坡

branches.en: A place whose way in actually works.
branches.cn: 入口真正行得通的场所。

branches.en: A service or price within most people's reach.
branches.cn: 多数人够得着的服务或价格。

branches.en: Writing clear enough for a non-specialist.
branches.cn: 非专业者也能读懂的写作。

branches.en: A building with no physical barrier for disabled users.
branches.cn: 对残障使用者没有物理障碍的建筑。

branches.en: The general sense and the design sense both remove obstacles.
branches.cn: 一般义与设计义都在消除障碍。

intro.en: The word joins the going root ced- with the prefix ad- and the possibility suffix -ible, and its family adds noun and adverb forms.
intro.cn: 这个词把「走」词根 ced- 与前缀 ad-、可能性后缀 -ible 结合，词族另加名词与副词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin accedere plus -ibilis produced the form, so the Latin entries record the verb and the suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accedere 加 -ibilis 构成此形，因此拉丁条目记录动词与后缀。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「可及性；无障碍程度」
副词，义为「易懂地」

definition_zh: 配件；饰品；附件；从犯；附加的
definition_en: an extra item that completes something, or a person who helps another commit a crime
core_image: 一套衣服之外再添的一条围巾、一只包
scene: 她穿素色长裙，只加了一枚旧胸针，整个造型立刻完整。A simple brooch was her only accessory.
sceneCN: 这里 accessory 是「饰品、配件」（第 1 个义项：起补充作用的附加物件）；句意为一枚简单的胸针是她唯一的配饰。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀构成，义为「搭配饰物」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「配以饰物的」

senses.title: An extra item that completes a look
senses.definition: an item such as a bag, belt, or jewellery worn to complete an outfit
senses.definitionCN: 包、腰带或首饰之类，用来完善整体装束的物件
senses.example: She keeps her accessories simple: one ring and a plain scarf.
senses.exampleCN: 她的配饰很简单：一枚戒指和一条素色围巾。
senses.why: Latin accessorius meant 'that which comes alongside'; an accessory stands beside the main thing and completes it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessorius 意为「随之而来的」；配件站在主物旁边，把它补充完整。

senses.title: An additional part for a device
senses.definition: an optional part that adds function to a machine or tool
senses.definitionCN: 为机器或工具增加功能的可选部件
senses.example: The shop sells lenses and other camera accessories.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售镜头与其他相机配件。
senses.why: The same 'coming alongside' logic applies to machines: the part does not work alone but extends what the main device can do.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「在旁边」逻辑适用于机器：配件不能单独工作，只是扩展主设备的功能。

senses.title: A person who helps in a crime
senses.definition: a person who assists another in committing an offence without being the principal
senses.definitionCN: 协助他人实施犯罪、但非主犯的人
senses.example: He was charged as an accessory to the robbery.
senses.exampleCN: 他被指控为抢劫案的从犯。
senses.why: Legal Latin used accessorius for a person standing beside the main actor, so the criminal sense keeps the idea of help from the side.
senses.whyCN: 法律拉丁语用 accessorius 指站在主行为人旁边的人，因此罪案义保留了「从旁协助」的意思。

senses.title: Additional and subordinate
senses.definition: existing to support something more important
senses.definitionCN: 为支持更重要之物而存在
senses.example: The firm treats training as an accessory service, not a core one.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司把培训当作附加服务，而非核心业务。
senses.why: The adjective generalizes the noun: anything that only supports a main thing can be called accessory.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把名词一般化：任何只起支持主物作用的东西都可称为附加的。

intro.en: Accessory comes from Latin accessorius, 'that which comes alongside', from accedere, 'to go toward'.
intro.cn: accessory 来自拉丁语 accessorius（随之而来的），源自动词 accedere（走向）。

items.en: cedere meant 'to go', the root behind access and accede.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走」，是 access 与 accede 的词根。

items.en: accedere meant 'to go toward, come alongside'.
items.cn: accedere 意为「走向、从旁而来」。

items.en: accessor named a person who comes alongside, often as a helper.
items.cn: accessor 指从旁而来的人，常为帮手。

items.en: accessorius meant 'belonging to one who comes alongside'.
items.cn: accessorius 意为「属于从旁而来者的」。

items.en: English accessory first appeared in legal language for a helper in a case.
items.cn: 英语 accessory 先出现在法律语言中，指案中帮手。

items.en: Modern usage adds clothing items and optional device parts.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了服饰单品与可选设备部件。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb and participle from the same family; the second gathers words for added items and helpers.
note.cn: 第一组收同族动词与分词；第二组收表示附加物与帮手的词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to add accessories to an outfit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「给装束搭配饰物」。

entries.definition: An adjective for an outfit completed with accessories.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「配以饰物的」。

entries.definition: The noun and verb for a way in or the act of reaching.
entries.definitionCN: 名词与动词，义为「通道」或「访问」。

entries.definition: An extra part fixed to a device.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附加装置」，固定在设备上的部件。

entries.definition: Something added to improve or complete.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附加物」，为改进或完善而添加。

entries.definition: A person who helps another commit a crime.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「共犯」，协助他人犯罪的人。

entries.definition: An item added for beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「装饰品」，为美观而添加。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'comes alongside' origin and the fashion phrases; the abstract hooks picture a plain dress completed by one brooch.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「从旁而来」来源与服饰搭配；抽象记忆点想象一枚胸针补全素色长裙。

normal.en: Accessory is Latin 'comes alongside' the main thing.
normal.cn: accessory 是拉丁语「从旁而来」，伴随主物。

normal.en: Fashion accessories and car accessories are the two shopping phrases.
normal.cn: fashion accessories 与 car accessories 是两个购物短语。

normal.en: An accessory to a crime is a helper, not the main actor.
normal.cn: an accessory to a crime 是帮凶，不是主犯。

normal.en: The plural is accessories, and the verb is accessorize.
normal.cn: 复数是 accessories，动词是 accessorize。

normal.en: Accessory as an adjective means subordinate or supporting.
normal.cn: accessory 作形容词意为附属的、辅助的。

abstract.en: Picture a plain dress completed by one old brooch.
abstract.cn: 想象素色长裙因一枚旧胸针而完整。

abstract.en: Picture a camera with an extra lens clipped on.
abstract.cn: 想象相机上多挂了一支镜头。

abstract.en: Picture a driver waiting outside while another enters the bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在外开车等候，另一人进银行。

examples.en: The belt is sold as an accessory, not part of the suit.
examples.cn: 这条腰带作为配件出售，不含在套装内。

examples.en: Phone accessories fill two shelves in the shop.
examples.cn: 手机配件占了店里两个货架。

examples.en: He was convicted as an accessory to the fraud.
examples.cn: 他作为诈骗案的从犯被定罪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞瑟瑞」——站在主物旁边、给它补上最后一笔的小物件，就是配件。

root: 拉丁语 accedere（从旁而来）+ -orius（属于……的）；核心义是「从旁补充主物之物」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a worn item that completes an outfit, to an optional device part, to a person who helps in a crime, to the general adjective 'supporting'.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从完善装束的佩戴物，走到可选的设备部件，再到罪案中的帮手，最后是形容词「附属的」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small item standing beside the main thing
core.cn: 核心意象：站在主物旁边的一件小物

branches.en: A worn item that finishes an outfit.
branches.cn: 完成整套装束的佩戴物。

branches.en: An optional part that extends a device.
branches.cn: 扩展设备功能的可选部件。

branches.en: A person who assists the main actor in a crime.
branches.cn: 在犯罪中协助主行为人者。

branches.en: Anything that only supports something more important.
branches.cn: 任何只支持更重要之物的东西。

branches.en: Fashion and hardware both add a piece beside the main item.
branches.cn: 服饰与硬件都在主物旁添加一件东西。

intro.en: The word joins the going root ced- with the prefix ad- and the relational ending -ory, and its family adds a verb and participle.
intro.cn: 这个词把「走」词根 ced- 与前缀 ad-、关系后缀 -ory 结合，词族另加动词与分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin accessorius is the direct ancestor, formed from accessor, so the Latin entries record the noun and the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accessorius 是直接祖先，由 accessor 构成，因此拉丁条目记录名词与形容词。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「搭配饰物」
形容词，义为「配以饰物的」

definition_zh: 事故；意外；偶然；巧合
definition_en: an unexpected event that causes damage or injury, or something happening by chance
core_image: 车道上突然滑出的一道痕，本来什么都不该发生
scene: 雨后的路口，两辆车因为刹车打滑轻轻撞在一起，所幸没人受伤。The accident blocked one lane for an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 accident 是「事故」（第 1 个义项：造成损失或伤害的意外事件）；句意为这起事故让一条车道受阻一小时。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「意外的；偶然的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「意外地；不小心地」

senses.title: An unexpected harmful event
senses.definition: an event that happens without being planned and causes injury or damage
senses.definitionCN: 未预料而发生、造成伤害或损失的事件
senses.example: The factory accident injured two workers.
senses.exampleCN: 这次工厂事故伤了两名工人。
senses.why: Latin accidere meant 'to happen, to fall upon'; an event that falls upon people unplanned became the everyday word for a mishap.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accidere 意为「发生、落到」（ad- 加 cadere「落下」）；落到人身上的未预料事件成了「事故」的日常用词。

senses.title: A road crash
senses.definition: a collision involving vehicles, usually with damage or injury
senses.definitionCN: 涉及车辆的碰撞，通常造成损坏或伤害
senses.example: There was an accident at the junction this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今天早上交叉路口发生了交通事故。
senses.why: As vehicles became common, the most visible kind of mishap was the collision, so the general word narrowed in daily speech.
senses.whyCN: 随着车辆普及，最显眼的意外就是碰撞，于是这个泛称在日常口语中以交通事故为主。

senses.title: Chance rather than plan
senses.definition: the way something happens without being intended or arranged
senses.definitionCN: 某事未经有意安排而发生的方式
senses.example: I found the letter by accident while cleaning the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 我清理抽屉时偶然找到了那封信。
senses.why: Before it named disasters, accident simply meant 'a happening'; the old neutral sense survives in by accident.
senses.whyCN: 在指灾祸之前，accident 只表示「发生之事」；这一中性旧义残存在 by accident 中。

intro.en: Accident comes from Latin accidere, 'to happen', literally 'to fall upon'.
intro.cn: accident 来自拉丁语 accidere（发生），字面意为「落到」。

items.en: cadere meant 'to fall', the root of case, incident, and decay.
items.cn: cadere 意为「落下」，是 case、incident 与 decay 的词根。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant 'to, toward'.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「向」。

items.en: accidere meant 'to fall upon, happen to'.
items.cn: accidere 意为「落到、发生于」。

items.en: The participle accidens named something that happens, a chance attribute.
items.cn: 分词 accidens 指发生之事，即偶然的附属属性。

items.en: Old French accident narrowed toward an unlucky event.
items.cn: 古法语 accident 词义收窄为不幸事件。

items.en: English accident first meant any happening, then a harmful one.
items.cn: 英语 accident 先指任何发生之事，后指有害之事。

note.en: The first group gathers the adjective, adverb, and the plural; the second gathers words for mishaps and chance.
note.cn: 第一组收形容词、副词与复数；第二组收表示意外与偶然的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning happening by chance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「偶然的、意外的」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'without intending to'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「意外地、不小心地」。

entries.definition: An event, often unpleasant, from the same Latin falling root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件（常指不愉快的）」，同出拉丁语「落下」。

entries.definition: A particular time or event, from the same family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时刻、场合」，同族词。

entries.definition: A violent collision of vehicles or objects.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「碰撞、撞车」。

entries.definition: A small accident without serious damage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小意外」，损坏不严重。

entries.definition: The act of two moving bodies striking each other.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「碰撞」。

entries.definition: Two events happening at once by chance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「巧合」，两件事同时偶然发生。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin 'falls upon' image and the by-pattern; the abstract hooks picture a wet road and one skid mark.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁语「落到」意象与 by 结构；抽象记忆点想象湿路面与一道刹车痕。

normal.en: Accident is Latin 'falls upon': cadere means to fall.
normal.cn: accident 是拉丁语「落到」：cadere 意为落下。

normal.en: By accident is the fixed phrase for chance.
normal.cn: by accident 是表示偶然的固定短语。

normal.en: Traffic accident is the everyday compound.
normal.cn: traffic accident 是日常复合说法。

normal.en: The adjective is accidental, the adverb accidentally.
normal.cn: 形容词是 accidental，副词是 accidentally。

normal.en: No accident means it was clearly intended.
normal.cn: no accident 意为显然是刻意为之。

abstract.en: Picture a wet junction with one long skid mark.
abstract.cn: 想象湿滑路口上一道长长的刹车痕。

abstract.en: Picture a letter slipping out of an old drawer by chance.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信偶然从旧抽屉滑出。

abstract.en: Picture two strangers reaching for the same book at once.
abstract.cn: 想象两个陌生人同时伸手拿同一本书。

examples.en: The accident happened because the driver fell asleep.
examples.cn: 事故因司机睡着而发生。

examples.en: She broke the glass by accident.
examples.cn: 她不小心打碎了玻璃杯。

examples.en: It was no accident that the two reports reached the same conclusion.
examples.cn: 两份报告得出同一结论并非偶然。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克西登特」——本该什么都不发生，偏偏有东西落到你头上，就是意外。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ cadere（落下）→ accidere（落到、发生）；核心义是「未预料落到身上的事」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from any harmful unplanned event, to the road crash as its commonest form, to the old neutral sense of chance.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从任何有害的未预料事件，走到其最常见形态的交通事故，再到古老中性的「偶然」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something falling on you when nothing was planned
core.cn: 核心意象：什么都没安排，却有东西落到你身上

branches.en: An unplanned event that leaves injury or damage.
branches.cn: 留下伤害或损失的未预料事件。

branches.en: The vehicle collision that dominates daily speech.
branches.cn: 在日常语言中占主导的车辆碰撞。

branches.en: The old neutral sense of something simply happening.
branches.cn: 古老中性的「事情发生」义。

branches.en: The general mishap and the road crash are the same word.
branches.cn: 一般意外与交通事故是同一个词。

branches.en: Chance is the mechanism; harm is the frequent result.
branches.cn: 偶然是机制，伤害是常见结果。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin prefix ad- with the falling root cad-, and its family adds adjective and adverb endings.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与「落下」词根 cad- 结合，词族另加形容词与副词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin accidere and accidens are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the verb and the participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accidere 与 accidens 是直接祖先，因此拉丁条目记录动词与分词。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「意外的；偶然的」
副词，义为「意外地；不小心地」

definition_zh: 赞誉；称赞；欢呼拥立
definition_en: to praise someone or something enthusiastically in public, or the praise so given
core_image: 一群人同时喊出一个名字，掌声盖过其他声音
scene: 影片首映结束，全场起立鼓掌，评论在第二天铺满报纸。The film was acclaimed by critics on both sides of the Atlantic.
sceneCN: 这里 acclaim 是「称赞、赞誉」（第 1 个义项：公开而热烈地赞扬）；句意为这部影片受到大西洋两岸评论家的赞誉。

pos.zh: 称赞；热烈欢迎；欢呼拥立

derivatives.zh: 由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「广受赞誉的」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「欢呼；口头表决通过」

senses.title: To praise enthusiastically in public
senses.definition: to express strong public approval of a person, book, film, or performance
senses.definitionCN: 公开表达对人、书、影片或演出的强烈赞许
senses.example: Critics acclaimed the novel as a rare achievement.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞这部小说是难得的成就。
senses.why: Latin acclamare meant 'to shout to'; praise first had to be shouted aloud, and the modern verb keeps that public volume.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acclamare 意为「向……喊」；赞誉最初必须高声喊出，现代动词仍保留这份公开的响度。

senses.title: Public praise as a noun
senses.definition: the enthusiastic approval that a work or person receives
senses.definitionCN: 作品或人所获得的热情认可
senses.example: The play opened to widespread acclaim.
senses.exampleCN: 这部戏一上演就广受赞誉。
senses.why: Once the shouting is over, the noun names the reputation left behind, so critical acclaim is a standing verdict.
senses.whyCN: 喊声过去之后，名词指留下的名声，因此 critical acclaim 是一种持续的评价。

senses.title: To hail someone formally
senses.definition: to declare someone a ruler or winner by general shouting, in older or ceremonial use
senses.definitionCN: 旧时或仪式中，以众人呼声宣布某人为统治者或胜者
senses.example: The army acclaimed him emperor at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 军队在城门前欢呼拥立他为皇帝。
senses.why: The oldest use is political: a crowd's shout made a proclamation, and the word still can name that ceremony.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法是政治的：众人的呼喊本身就是宣告，这个词如今仍可指那种仪式。

intro.en: Acclaim comes from Latin acclamare, 'to shout at', built from ad- and clamare, 'to cry out'.
intro.cn: acclaim 来自拉丁语 acclamare（向……喊），由 ad- 与 clamare（呼喊）构成。

items.en: clamare meant 'to cry out', the source of clamour and exclaim.
items.cn: clamare 意为「呼喊」，是 clamour 与 exclaim 的来源。

items.en: acclamare meant 'to shout at, cry out in approval'.
items.cn: acclamare 意为「向……喊、以呼喊表示赞同」。

items.en: acclamatio named a shout of approval, including in Roman elections.
items.cn: acclamatio 指赞同的呼喊，也用于罗马选举。

items.en: French acclamer carried the public praise sense forward.
items.cn: 法语 acclamer 延续公开赞誉义。

items.en: English acclaim first meant to shout approval or hail a ruler.
items.cn: 英语 acclaim 最初指呼喊赞同或拥立统治者。

items.en: Modern usage centres on praise of art and achievement.
items.cn: 现代用法集中在艺术与成就的赞誉。

note.en: The first group gathers the participle adjective, the noun, and the shouting verb; the second gathers words for praise.
note.cn: 第一组收分词形容词、名词与同源「呼喊」动词；第二组收表示赞扬的词。

entries.definition: An adjective for a work widely praised.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「广受赞誉的」。

entries.definition: A shout of approval or a vote by cheering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「欢呼、以呼声表决」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to cry out suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「突然呼喊」，同出拉丁语 clamare。

entries.definition: A loud confused noise or a demand shouted by many.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「喧闹、呼声」。

entries.definition: A general word for expressing approval.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「赞扬」，泛指表示赞许。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to clap or approve strongly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「鼓掌、赞许」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to honour something publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「颂扬、庆祝」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to greet or announce as great.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欢呼、称颂」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin shouting root and the film phrases; the abstract hooks picture a hall rising to applaud.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁语「呼喊」词根与影评搭配；抽象记忆点想象全场起立鼓掌。

normal.en: Acclaim is ad- plus clamare, 'to shout': praise shouted aloud.
normal.cn: acclaim 是 ad- 加 clamare（呼喊）：高声喊出的赞誉。

normal.en: Critical acclaim and international acclaim are the two review phrases.
normal.cn: critical acclaim 与 international acclaim 是两个评论短语。

normal.en: Be acclaimed as means to be publicly called something.
normal.cn: be acclaimed as 意为被公开称为某种成就。

normal.en: The adjective is acclaimed, as in a much acclaimed film.
normal.cn: 形容词是 acclaimed，如 a much acclaimed film。

normal.en: The noun acclamation also names a vote by cheering.
normal.cn: 名词 acclamation 也指以欢呼进行的表决。

abstract.en: Picture a whole hall rising to clap at once.
abstract.cn: 想象整个大厅同时起立鼓掌。

abstract.en: Picture a name shouted repeatedly until it fills the street.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被反复喊到充满街道。

abstract.en: Picture an army at a gate declaring a general emperor.
abstract.cn: 想象军队在城门前宣布将军为皇帝。

examples.en: The documentary was acclaimed for its honesty.
examples.cn: 这部纪录片因坦诚而受到赞誉。

examples.en: Her debut novel won wide critical acclaim.
examples.cn: 她的处女作小说赢得评论界广泛赞誉。

examples.en: The crowd acclaimed the winner as a hero.
examples.cn: 人群欢呼称胜者为英雄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克莱姆」——全场同时喊出一个名字，那就是赞誉。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ clamare（呼喊）→ acclamare（向……喊）；核心义是「公开而热烈地喊出赞许」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from public praise shouted at a work, to the reputation it leaves, to the older ceremony of hailing a ruler.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从公开对作品喊出赞许，走到由此留下的名声，再到旧时拥立统治者的仪式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd shouting one name in unison
core.cn: 核心意象：众人齐声喊出同一个名字

branches.en: Strong public approval shouted at a work or person.
branches.cn: 对作品或人高声表达的强烈公开赞许。

branches.en: The reputation that remains after the shouting.
branches.cn: 喊声过后留下的名声。

branches.en: The old ceremony of declaring a ruler by acclamation.
branches.cn: 以呼声宣布统治者的古老仪式。

branches.en: The shout and the reputation are the event and its trace.
branches.cn: 呼喊与名声是事件与其痕迹。

branches.en: Political hailing and artistic praise share one loud public voice.
branches.cn: 政治拥立与艺术赞誉共享同一种响亮的公共声音。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin prefix ad- with the shouting root clam-, and its family adds the participle, action noun, and related verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与「呼喊」词根 clam- 结合，词族另加分词、动作名词与相关动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin acclamare and acclamatio are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the verb and its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 acclamare 与 acclamatio 是直接祖先，因此拉丁条目记录动词与其名词。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「广受赞誉的」
名词，义为「欢呼；口头表决通过」

definition_zh: （英）适应新气候；服水土；适应新环境
definition_en: to become used to a new climate or conditions, especially gradually
core_image: 身体在几周里慢慢学会呼吸稀薄的空气
scene: 登山队在四千米营地住了十天，每天只爬高一点，等身体适应了才继续上去。The team stayed at base camp to acclimatise before the summit push.
sceneCN: 这里 acclimatise 是「适应新气候、服水土」（第 1 个义项：身体逐渐习惯新的气候条件）；句意为队伍留在营地以适应环境，再冲顶。

pos.zh: 适应气候；服水土；适应新环境

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「适应气候的过程」
由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「已适应水土的」

senses.title: To get used to a new climate
senses.definition: of a person, animal, or plant, to become adjusted to a different climate
senses.definitionCN: 指人或动植物逐渐习惯不同的气候
senses.example: It took her a month to acclimatise to the humid summer.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了一个月才适应潮湿的夏天。
senses.why: The word joins a- 'to' with climate, so it literally means 'to bring into a climate'; the body slowly learns the new air.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 a-（向）与 climate 构成，字面是「使进入某种气候」；身体慢慢学会新的空气。

senses.title: To adjust to high altitude
senses.definition: to let the body adjust to thinner air before heavy exertion
senses.definitionCN: 在剧烈活动前让身体适应稀薄空气
senses.example: Climbers must acclimatise before going above the snow line.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者越过雪线前必须先适应高海拔。
senses.why: Thin air is the sharpest test of climate adjustment, so mountaineering made this the word's best known use.
senses.whyCN: 稀薄空气是对气候适应最严峻的考验，因此登山使这一用法最为人熟知。

senses.title: To adapt to a new setting
senses.definition: to become comfortable with unfamiliar habits, work, or surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐习惯陌生的习惯、工作或环境
senses.example: New staff need time to acclimatise to the office culture.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工需要时间适应办公室文化。
senses.why: Once the body's adjustment became a model, the verb extended to any slow settling into unfamiliar conditions.
senses.whyCN: 身体的调适一旦成为模型，这个动词就扩展到任何慢慢安顿进陌生条件的过程。

intro.en: Acclimatise is built from the French verb acclimater plus the -ise ending, with climate at its centre.
intro.cn: acclimatise 由法语动词 acclimater 加 -ise 后缀构成，核心是 climate。

items.en: klima meant 'slope, zone', and it named the bands of the earth by latitude.
items.cn: klima 意为「斜坡、地带」，按纬度命名地球上的气候带。

items.en: clima meant a region or zone of the earth.
items.cn: clima 指地球上的区域或地带。

items.en: French climat narrowed the sense to weather conditions.
items.cn: 法语 climat 词义收窄为天气状况。

items.en: acclimater meant 'to accustom to a climate'.
items.cn: acclimater 意为「使适应气候」。

items.en: English formed acclimatise from the French verb for plants and settlers.
items.cn: 英语由该法语动词构成 acclimatise，用于植物与移居者。

items.en: Modern usage extends it to altitude and to any unfamiliar setting.
items.cn: 现代用法把它扩展到高海拔与任何陌生环境。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun and participle and the American spelling; the second gathers verbs for gradual adjustment.

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the climate core and the climb phrases; the abstract hooks picture lungs learning thin air day by day.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 climate 核心与登山搭配；抽象记忆点想象肺一天天学会稀薄空气。

normal.en: Acclimatise has climate inside it: to enter a new climate.
normal.cn: acclimatise 内含 climate：进入新的气候。

normal.en: Acclimatise to is the usual pattern.
normal.cn: acclimatise to 是常见结构。

normal.en: Mountaineers acclimatise to altitude before a summit push.
normal.cn: 登山者在冲顶前适应高海拔。

normal.en: The noun is acclimatisation, spelled with -isation in British use.
normal.cn: 名词是 acclimatisation，英式拼写用 -isation。

normal.en: The American spelling is acclimatize.
normal.cn: 美式拼写是 acclimatize。

abstract.en: Picture a tent at base camp and slow walks uphill each day.
abstract.cn: 想象大本营的帐篷与每天缓慢向上走。

abstract.en: Picture a newcomer fanning herself through a first humid week.
abstract.cn: 想象新来者在第一个潮湿的星期里不停扇风。

abstract.en: Picture a seedling moved outdoors and hardening over weeks.
abstract.cn: 想象幼苗被移到户外，几周里逐渐强韧。

examples.en: The plants need a season to acclimatise to the colder garden.
examples.cn: 这些植物需要一季来适应更冷的花园。

examples.en: Give yourself two days to acclimatise to the time change.
examples.cn: 给自己两天适应时差。

examples.en: The expedition acclimatised at the camp for nine days.
examples.cn: 探险队在营地适应了九天。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from adjusting to a new climate, to the sharp case of thin mountain air, to settling into any unfamiliar setting.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从适应新气候，走到山地稀薄空气这一极端情形，再到安顿进任何陌生环境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body slowly learning to breathe unfamiliar air
core.cn: 核心意象：身体慢慢学会呼吸陌生的空气

branches.en: A person or plant adjusting to a different climate.
branches.cn: 人或植物适应不同气候。

branches.en: The body adjusting to thin air before exertion.
branches.cn: 身体在剧烈活动前适应稀薄空气。

branches.en: A newcomer settling into unfamiliar habits and work.
branches.cn: 新来者安顿进陌生习惯与工作。

branches.en: Altitude is the hardest version of climate adjustment.
branches.cn: 高海拔是气候适应中最难的版本。

branches.en: Both require time rather than force.
branches.cn: 两者都需要时间而非强求。

intro.en: The word joins the climate stem with a prefix and a verb ending, and its family adds the action noun and participle.
intro.cn: 这个词把 climate 词干与前缀、动词后缀结合，词族另加动作名词与分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin clima is the ancestor behind climate, and the -ise ending came from French -iser.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 clima 是 climate 背后的祖先，-ise 后缀来自法语 -iser。

definition_en: to become or make someone become used to a new climate or conditions

scene: 实验室把一批兰花先放进半阴棚里几周，再移植到温室，免得它们一次受寒。Growers acclimatize orchids slowly before moving them.
sceneCN: 这里 acclimatize 是「使适应气候」（第 1 个义项：让生物逐渐习惯新的气候条件）；句意为种植者把兰花缓慢移出以适应环境。

senses.title: To make someone or something used to a climate
senses.definition: to help a person, animal, or plant adjust to different weather conditions
senses.definitionCN: 帮助人或动植物调适到不同的天气条件
senses.example: Gardeners acclimatize young trees by moving them outdoors in stages.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁分阶段把幼树移到户外，让它适应。
senses.why: The -ize ending marks making or becoming; with climate as its base, the verb covers both 'to become used' and 'to make used'.
senses.whyCN: -ize 后缀表示「使……、变得」；以 climate 为词基，这个动词同时覆盖「变得适应」与「使适应」。

senses.title: To adjust to a new way of life
senses.definition: to become used to unfamiliar routines, food, or social habits
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐习惯陌生的作息、饮食或社会习惯
senses.example: Students from abroad take a term to acclimatize to local customs.
senses.exampleCN: 外国学生要一学期才能适应当地习俗。
senses.why: When the climate is social rather than physical, the same verb describes the slow warming up to a place's habits.
senses.whyCN: 当「气候」是社会性的而非物理性的，同一个动词描述对一个地方习惯的缓慢熟悉。

senses.title: To prepare equipment or data for new conditions
senses.titleCN: 使（设备、数据）适应新条件
senses.definition: to adjust instruments or records to a new environment or scale
senses.definitionCN: 使仪器或记录调整到新的环境或尺度
senses.example: The sensors were acclimatized to the desert heat before the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 勘测前，传感器已适应沙漠高温。
senses.why: Technical writing applies the biological model to instruments: hardware also needs a period of settling before it reads correctly.
senses.whyCN: 技术写作把生物模型用到仪器上：硬件也需要一段稳定期才能读数准确。

intro.en: Acclimatize pairs the climate stem with the -ize ending that marks making or becoming.
intro.cn: acclimatize 把 climate 词干与表示「使……、变得」的 -ize 后缀结合。

items.en: klima meant 'slope, zone', used for bands of the earth.
items.cn: klima 意为「斜坡、地带」，用于地球气候带。

items.en: clima meant a zone or region of the earth.
items.cn: clima 指地球上的地带或区域。

items.en: French climat came to mean the weather of a place.
items.cn: 法语 climat 转为指某地的天气。

items.en: acclimater meant 'to accustom to a climate', first used of plants.
items.cn: acclimater 意为「使适应气候」，最初用于植物。

items.en: English formed acclimatize with the -ize ending, matching the American style.
items.cn: 英语以 -ize 后缀构成 acclimatize，与美式风格一致。

items.en: Modern usage also covers social adjustment and instrument settling.
items.cn: 现代用法也覆盖社会性适应与仪器稳定。
